stories.headline: Rescuers say 39 missing after Indonesia factory fire
stories.deck: TV images taken overnight showed parts of the factory - described as a confectionery and sugar product manufacturer - on fire, with parts of its roof collapsed
stories.bodyText:
Indonesian rescue workers were searching for 39 missing people on Sunday (November 22, 2026) after a confectionery factory caught fire west of Jakarta, a rescue official said.
The Fonusa Agung Mulia factory, located in the Serang district around 50 kilometres (31 miles) from the capital, caught fire on Saturday afternoon, a local search and rescue agency said in a statement.
TV images taken overnight showed parts of the factory - described as a confectionery and sugar product manufacturer - on fire, with parts of its roof collapsed.
"As of now, 39 people are still being searched for," rescue official Rizky Dwianto said, adding that four others were injured.
Fires were still burning in parts of the factory on Sunday, complicating the search for missing victims, Mr. Rizky said.
"All elements of the joint SAR team are making maximum effort to locate the victims while prioritising the safety of personnel in the field," he added.
The cause of the incident is still under investigation, the local disaster agency said in an Instagram post Sunday.

stories.headline: Facebook, Kramnik-Leko and a 22-year wait: Switzerland prepares for Gukesh-Sindarov clash
stories.deck: Grandmaster Peter Leko’s dramatic clash against Vladimir Kramnik in 2004 was the last World Chess Championship hosted in Switzerland. During an exclusive interaction with TimesofIndia.com, the Hungarian chess veteran reflects on the psychological pressure, preparation challenges and dramatic final game of that encounter, while drawing parallels with the upcoming Gukesh–Sindarov title clash in…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: In the early days of social media, racking up a massive friend list was more of a competitive sport for many. A 2008 study by Jolene Zywica and James Danowski found that two-thirds of surveyed people knew someone actively padding their friend count just to look popular, while later research by psychologist Phillip Ozimek showed that materialistic users often collected online friends like digital trophies.
Oxford evolutionary psychologist Robin Dunbar, meanwhile, proved that out of hundreds of online connections, only about four actually count as close. But all this came to light because of Facebook, launched by Mark Zuckerberg as TheFacebook in 2004, a year that also gave the world Gmail and saw Google’s landmark initial public offering. But for chess fans, 2004 holds an entirely different resonance.
In a corner of southern Switzerland, along the shores of Lake Maggiore in the village of Brissago, Russian Grandmaster Vladimir Kramnik was defending his Classical World Chess Championship crown against Hungarian challenger Peter Leko.
For 22 years, Brissago stood as the last time Switzerland hosted a World Chess Championship match.
Now, as reigning champion Gukesh Dommaraju prepares to defend his title against Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov on Swiss soil (in Geneva this time), Leko, who will call the action as FIDE’s official commentator alongside Russian Grandmaster Peter Svidler, finds himself looking back at the quiet Alpine lakeside town where he came within a single game of immortality.
"Switzerland is an amazing place to play a World Championship match because it's very quiet and peaceful," Leko, now 47, recalled during an exclusive interview with TimesofIndia.com. "It lets the players focus fully on the championship without any disruptions. I had a wonderful time in Brissago, so I have very pleasant memories of the organisation and the whole environment."
Inside the Centro Dannemann, however, facing Kramnik in 2004 meant stepping into the ring with a champion considered untouchable, a man who had dethroned Garry Kasparov in 2000 without losing a single game.
"You also have to remember that those were the times before the computer era, before the strong engines," Leko shared with a smile. "Catching up with opening preparation was almost impossible. Kramnik had already played a World Championship match against Kasparov and had been a top-10 player since 1993, when I was still a child. He was way ahead in opening preparation, and that was a big handicap during the match."
That preparation gap exploded onto the board immediately. Leko lost the very first game with the white pieces. Under the rules of the era, it looked close to fatal.
The 2004 championship was the final title match in history played under the old draw-odds stipulation, meaning if the 14-game contest ended in a 7–7 tie, the title holder would retain the crown.
Leko remembers the post-game press conference, where a reporter asked him whether he still believed he had any chance after the opening loss, or why the match was even worth continuing.
"I became very angry because I felt that there was a reason why I had lost that first game with the white pieces," Leko recalled. "First of all, Kramnik had very good preparation, which was actually based on a queen sacrifice to force a draw and establish a fortress. However, as a young challenger, I felt that the whole world was watching, so I had to keep fighting. I tried to push too hard, and it backfired."
Trailing by a full point against an undefeated champion with an extra white game still to come, Leko realised that survival depended on leaning completely on his seconds. But how did he do that?
"That is a very good question," he smiled again. "I realised that I had to forget about what people were thinking or saying. I had to focus only on myself, my game, and my team. That was absolutely the right decision. I completely shut myself off from outside noise and expectations. I just wanted to prove to myself that I had a chance."
Leko, with white pieces, had spent months preparing to dismantle Kramnik’s famed Berlin Defence against 1.e4.
But in the match, Kramnik ambushed him with an airtight Petroff Defence that neutralised everything Leko had built. Over the next three games, draws dominated the scene.
In Game 5, Leko abandoned his primary weapon altogether and opened with 1.d4, stepping straight into Kramnik’s own signature territory.
"Even today, with computers, it's difficult to switch from 1.e4 to 1.d4," Leko said. "But more than 20 years ago, when experience and time mattered so much, it was a huge challenge to transfer my game to 1.d4 during the match. I managed to win the fifth game with my 1.d4 and tie the match. That was like a miracle. After that, I knew I would have all the chances. My advantage was that he didn't know how much I knew."
Leko surged ahead in Game 8 with a celebrated victory using the Marshall Attack with Black and entered the 14th and final game needing only a draw to become World Champion.
Kramnik, cornered and desperate, conjured a masterpiece in the final round to level the score at 7–7 and retain his title on the draw rule.
"Of course, when I lost the last game and the match ended 7–7, it felt like a big tragedy," Leko reminisced.
"It hurt very much because I was so close to becoming World Champion. But looking back, I'm extremely proud to have had the chance to play that match with Kramnik and make it 7–7, because Kramnik was considered invincible in those days."
Two decades later, 
Leko sees those exact psychological currents, mostly hype, hidden preparation, and the weight of expectation, shaping the Gukesh–Sindarov showdown in Switzerland
.

stories.headline: Two Patriot radars hit? Iran launches missile-drone attack on US bases in Bahrain
stories.bodyText:
Bahrain has reported an Iranian attack on a civilian industrial facility, triggering a fire and causing material damage, as tensions escalate across the Gulf amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. The incident came as Tehran claimed that its forces had targeted two United States Patriot air defence radars at military bases in Bahrain.
Bahrain’s ministry of interior said preliminary reports indicated material damage but no casualties. Civil defence teams were deployed to bring the fire under control, the ministry said in a post on X, describing the incident as part of “Iranian aggression”.
The ministry did not identify the industrial facility or disclose its location. The incident came after air raid sirens sounded across Bahrain, with authorities urging residents to move to the nearest safe place without initially specifying the nature of the threat.
Bahrain’s defence force said its air defence systems had intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks late on Saturday.
In a separate statement, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed responsibility for a combined missile and drone operation targeting US military positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain.
According to a statement broadcast by Iranian state broadcaster IRIB and reported by Al Jazeera, the IRGC Aerospace Force targeted two Patriot air defence radars at the installations, claiming that both had been destroyed.
The IRGC described the operation as a response to what it called continued violations of Iranian airspace by American military drones.
“After two US MQ-1 and MQ-9 reconnaissance and combat drones violated Iranian airspace, US military positions at the aforementioned bases were targeted in an operation by the IRGC Aerospace Force,” the statement said.
The Iranian force also cited an alleged US attack on a radar installation on Iran’s Hengam Island as justification for its retaliatory action.
Earlier, Iranian state broadcaster IRIB released footage purportedly showing two US military drones, an MQ-9 and an MQ-1, being brought down over the Strait of Hormuz. Another video reportedly showed the missile and drone operation against the Patriot radar installations in Bahrain.
The footage also carried a message challenging US Central Command (CENTCOM) to issue another fact-check denying damage to American military equipment or claiming that it had not been targeted.
Meanwhile, Iran’s semi-official Fars news agency reported that the IRGC had attacked two military bases used by US forces at Sheikh Isa and Juffair.
Iran’s state news agency IRNA separately reported that an interceptor missile launched from the US Fifth Fleet base in Bahrain had crashed on Sitra Island, triggering a large fire. Citing Bahrain News, it attributed the incident to a recurring malfunction in the Patriot air defence system. This account was not independently established.
Bahrain hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet and has faced repeated attacks since the US-Israel war on Iran began in late February, including three drone attacks in recent days after a lull of several weeks.

stories.headline: Key takeaways from the Quad, ASEAN-India, and East Asia Summits in Manila | Explained
stories.deck: Narendra Modi’s multilateral ASEAN engagements showed a growing desire to work more closely with the grouping at a time when global powers are working in a more unilateral manner
stories.bodyText:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi took part in three back-to-back multilateral meetings on the sidelines of the annual Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) summits in Manila this week. The ASEAN-India Summit, East Asia Summit, and Quad Summit, which was attended by U.S. President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese apart from Mr. Modi, ended with several concrete announcements. They sent a deeper underlying message on India’s broad-basing of its “Act East” and Indo-Pacific policies, even as the world turned its attention to the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral later in the week.
In 2025, Mr. Modi skipped the ASEAN summits in Kuala Lumpur over what was seen as a combination of domestic commitments around Deepavali and trade friction with U.S. President Donald Trump.

stories.headline: Jharkhand CM writes to CJI, seeks urgent appointment of successor to HC Chief Justice M S Sonak
stories.bodyText:
Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren
Credit: PTI Photo
Ranchi: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren has urged Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and the Supreme Court Collegium to urgently recommend a successor to High Court Chief Justice M S Sonak, who is due to retire on November 27.
Experience a more refined e-paper today
In a letter to the CJI and judges of the Collegium, Soren said prolonged interim arrangements could create uncertainty within the judicial establishment.
The CM said frequent transitions disrupt administrative continuity and institutional planning in the high court.
Soren also sought a stable judicial leadership in the Jharkhand High Court to maintain public confidence in the justice delivery system.
“Without the Collegium's immediate action, the High Court of Jharkhand faces the prospect of yet another interim Acting Chief Justice arrangement… I hope it (the Collegium) will not disagree with me that the office of the Chief Justice is central to the administrative and judicial functioning of a high court,” he said in the letter.
“… As the head of the state government, I am compelled to draw your attention to the fact that an incoming Chief Justice has not been designated nor has any Hon’ble Justice been transferred to the Jharkhand High Court in advance… on the superannuation of Hon'ble Chief Justice M S Sonak on November 27, 2026,” Soren said.
Prior to the appointment of the incumbent Chief Justice on January 9, the high court has been “adorned by four Chief Justices since the superannuation of Justice Ravi Ranjan on December 19, 2022… one of His Lordships having a term of a fortnight”, the chief minister said in his letter to the CJI.
“During this period, Acting Chief Justices have been appointed on three occasions for terms ranging from two months to six months. I must, in my own humble way, express utmost respect and admiration for the foresight and dedication shown by the Collegium earlier this year to strengthen institutional continuity and judicial administration in its Statement of February 26, 2026,” he said.
Soren cited the Collegium’s decision that to strengthen the efficiency and quality of administration of justice, a judge proposed to take over the high court as its Chief Justice may be transferred well in advance, preferably two months before the vacancy arises, so that the recommendee becomes well conversant with the high court's affairs.
“The Collegium will appreciate that frequent transitions accompanied by extended interim arrangements disrupt administrative continuity, affect institutional planning and create uncertainty within the judicial establishment,” he added.

briefs.headline: At least nine killed, several injured as vehicle carrying pilgrims rams into truck in Rajasthan’s Kota
briefs.deck: According to Additional District Collector Rajesh Joshi, the vehicle was carrying 16 people who were returning to Maharashtra after visiting Khatu Shyam when the accident occurred in the middle of the night
briefs.bodyText:
At least nine people were killed and several others injured after a vehicle carrying pilgrims rammed into a parked truck near Shambhupura on the Kota-Udaipur highway in Rajasthan's Kota district, police said.
According to Additional District Collector Rajesh Joshi, the vehicle was carrying 16 people who were returning to Maharashtra after visiting Khatu Shyam when the accident occurred in the middle of the night. Describing the incident as tragic, Mr. Joshi said that all the occupants belonged to the same family.
"Near Shambhupura, a vehicle carrying 16 people collided with a truck in the middle of the night. It was a deeply tragic and painful accident, in which 9 people lost their lives. They were returning to Maharashtra after visiting Khatu Shyam. All of them were from the same family," he told ANI.
Mr. Joshi said the immediate priority of the administration was to ensure proper medical treatment for those injured in the accident."Our priority right now is ensuring that the injured receive proper medical care and recover. Meanwhile, the post-mortem procedures are being carried out for those who lost their lives in the accident," he added.

briefs.headline: Russian ‘triple-tap’ strike on Zelenskyy’s hometown kills child, wounds 60
briefs.bodyText:
A Russian ballistic missile attack on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s hometown of Kryvyi Rih killed two people, including a seven-year-old boy, and wounded 60 others, including six children, local officials said on Saturday. Emergency crews came under further strikes as they responded to the initial assault.
The attack took place on Friday night in the central Ukrainian city. Oleksandr Vilkul, head of the city administration, said a 20-year-old woman was also killed. Regional military administration chief Oleksandr Hanzha confirmed that 60 people had sustained injuries.
According to Vilkul, the strikes triggered four fires and damaged around 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools, an industrial facility, businesses and several vehicles.
Describing the sequence of attacks, Vilkul said Russian forces launched additional missiles after emergency personnel reached the site.
“First, two ballistic missiles. And then, when the emergency and rescue operation began, three more rockets hit doctors, rescuers and utility workers,” he wrote on Telegram.
Footage released by the regional branch of Ukraine’s State Emergency Service appeared to show further strikes as ambulance crews and firefighters were attending to the aftermath, with fires burning around them.
The attack comes amid uncertainty over US-mediated efforts to negotiate an end to the Russia-Ukraine war. It also followed reports of Russian missiles and a suspected drone entering Polish territory, prompting fresh concerns over regional security.
Nato Secretary-General Mark Rutte, speaking in Warsaw on Saturday, described the airspace violation as “dangerous” and said all alliance members stood “in full solidarity with Poland”.
“NATO will defend every inch of Polish territory,” Rutte said, adding that the alliance had responded appropriately by supporting Polish F-16 fighter jets with Nato aircraft.
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy defended Ukraine’s repeated strikes on the Kerch Bridge connecting occupied Crimea with mainland Russia, calling them a “fair response” to Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure.
“Not the number of missiles — the number of attacks,” he said, referring to Russian President Vladimir Putin's alleged 109 attacks on Ukrainian bridges.
Russian vessel hit by drones
Elsewhere, a Russian cargo ship, Sparta II, caught fire in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday after a drone strike suspected to have been carried out by Ukraine. Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said the war was spilling into Finland’s immediate neighbourhood, adding that Ukraine had the right to retaliate against Russian aggression.
The crew was evacuated to a nearby vessel and was expected to be taken back to Russia. Finnish authorities said firefighting operations were continuing off the southern town of Loviisa, with a Russian rescue ship assisting.

briefs.headline: Why Canadian billionaire Kevin O’Leary thinks Anthropic could be the next Amazon
briefs.deck: AI giant Anthropic has celebrated a milestone initial public offering, amassing a staggering $81.3 billion, which catapults its valuation to an impressive $1.5 trillion. Kevin O'Leary, an influential investor, commended the company's enterprise-driven approach focused on instilling trust and security among business clients. Notably, Amazon holds a substantial 14.7% share worth $225 billion, while…
briefs.bodyText:
AI giant Anthropic has found a powerful supporter in Canadian billionaire and Shark Tank investor Kevin O’Leary, who feels that the company’s enterprise-focused strategy could put it on a growth trajectory similar to that of 
Amazon
. The comments from O’Leary came as Anthropic made its blockbuster Nasdaq debut, raising a record $81.3 billion and achieving a valuation of about $1.5 trillion, making it one of the most closely watched AI companies on Wall Street. In a post shared on social media platform X on the day Anthropic began trading, O’Leary called the company’s strategy “sheer genius.” He argued that it has spotted something other AI players have overlooked: business customers will pay a premium for technology they can trust and keep secure.
Kevin O’Leary calls Anthropic’s AI approach ‘sheer genius’
O’Leary praised Anthropic’s focus on enterprise customers, and emphasised that the company has identified a key opportunity that many competitors have overlooked. As per the Shark Tank judge, businesses are ready to pay more on AI products that prioritise factors like trust, reliability and security. “Enterprise customers are willing to pay a premium for safety, security, and trust,” O’Leary wrote, describing Anthropic’s strategy as “sheer genius.”
The investor further added that strategy could help Anthropic in building a durable competitive advantage in the rapidly growing AI market, where enterprises are opting for secure solutions which can be deployed across critical business operations.
Why Kevin O’Leary compares Anthropic to Amazon
O’Leary drew parallels between Anthropic and Amazon, noting that exceptional growth can justify massive valuations even before a company reaches consistent profitability. He argued that Anthropic’s current expansion resembles Amazon’s early growth story, although he believes the AI company is advancing at a significantly faster pace. The comparison reflects growing investor optimism around AI firms that are rapidly scaling revenue while securing large corporate customers.
The record breaking IPO of Anthropic
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its marketed range of $70 to $78. The offering raised $81.3 billion, the largest on record, and values the company at about $1.5 trillion. Shares opened at $111.50 and rose to nearly $115. They closed 17.07% above the IPO price, then slipped 4.70% in after-hours trading. About 832 million shares changed hands, more than SpaceX’s first-day volume, making Anthropic the most actively traded stock on the Nasdaq.
Amazon and 
Google
 parent Alphabet are major investors. After the IPO, Amazon will reportedly hold 14.7% and Alphabet 13.7%, with Alphabet’s stake including $10 billion of shares bought in a private placement alongside the offering. Both companies also supply computing and other infrastructure to Anthropic.
Amazon’s stake in Anthropic: Almost 15% stake worth around $225 billion
Amazon has been one of Anthropic's biggest strategic partners since the AI company began building its Claude models. Apart from investing in Anthropic, Amazon has also supplied much of the computing infrastructure needed to develop and run its AI models. Amazon first invested in Anthropic in 2023. According to the company's IPO-related filing, Amazon now holds around 14.7% of Anthropic's total equity. At the $83 IPO price, this stake is worth approximately $225 billion.
Amazon's investment also involves convertible notes, which can be converted into shares. If all these notes were converted without the ownership limit, Amazon's stake could rise to 23.8% of Anthropic.
However, Amazon has chosen not to waive the ownership cap for the IPO. This means it will hold the smaller stake for now, while the remaining notes will be dealt with under the terms of the agreement.
Google’s stake in Anthropic: Around 13.7% stake worth nearly $200 billion
Alphabet-owned Google is another major beneficiary of Anthropic's public listing. The search giant owns around 13.7% of the AI company, a stake valued at approximately $200 billion at the $83 IPO price. Google's investment includes 135.1 million shares that it agreed to purchase for $10 billion through a private placement priced at the IPO rate.
For Google, Anthropic represents both an investment in a fast-growing AI company and a major customer for its cloud and computing services. The value of its holding could also change as Anthropic shares move in the public market.

briefs.headline: Brooklyn musician says landlord ignored cracks before collapse killed 8; sues
briefs.deck: In the wake of a devastating building collapse in Brooklyn that claimed eight lives, a musician has taken legal action against the landlord for ignoring warnings about visible cracks weeks prior. The lawsuit also raises alarms about nearby construction projects lacking proper structural support. Authorities are now probing the oversight of such projects in densely populated neighborhoods…
briefs.bodyText:
A Brooklyn musician who lost his home when a residential building in Flatbush collapsed, killing eight people, has filed a lawsuit alleging that he raised concerns about visible cracks weeks before the disaster but received no meaningful response from his landlord. The legal complaint also draws attention to construction plans for the neighbouring development, which reportedly did not provide for steel support beams at the precise section where the building eventually gave way. The allegations, first reported by Gothamist and subsequently covered by The Guardian and CBS News New York, have added another dimension to the investigation into the November 11 collapse at 1321 Flatbush Avenue.
The three-storey residential building fell into an adjoining construction site, leaving eight people dead and several others injured. The tenant, Dengane Omari Jack, a musician who had lived in the building for five years, filed his complaint in Brooklyn Supreme Court on November 16. According to the lawsuit, he noticed cracks around the building’s entrance in October, photographed them and alerted the landlord or property management.
Jack alleges that his concerns were dismissed rather than prompting an appropriate structural assessment. The complaint claims the landlord failed to arrange an inspection, organise necessary repairs or take protective measures despite the excavation work taking place immediately next door.
The lawsuit names the building’s landlord, Olufemi Falade, and several individuals and companies connected to the neighbouring development. These include the property’s ownership interests, construction contractors, a structural engineer and a special inspection firm. The claims have yet to be established in court.
The incident has also renewed questions about how construction activity is monitored in densely populated New York neighbourhoods, where excavation and redevelopment projects often take place alongside occupied residential buildings. 
The case is expected to draw attention to whether existing inspection procedures adequately protect neighbouring properties, particularly when residents report visible structural changes before construction-related work is completed. For those who lost family members or their homes in Flatbush, establishing whether the warning signs were overlooked remains central to the search for accountability.
The collapse occurred at around 4 pm on November 11, when the apartment building came down into the excavation site at 2625 Bedford Avenue. The incident also damaged the facade of another adjoining residential property. Emergency crews worked through the rubble as they searched for survivors, with the death toll eventually reaching eight, including two children.

briefs.headline: T.N. may see solar energy installations slowing down, say energy generators
briefs.deck: In the last one month, some of the solar energy generators received notices demanding 8% banking charges.
briefs.bodyText:
:
Tamil Nadu, which has 10,000 MW-11,000 MW of installed solar energy capacity, may see a slowdown in solar energy installations in 2027, according to industry representatives.
The single window system for obtaining approvals is not functioning effectively, finer details based on the recently-announced Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy should be notified by the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission, and costs are escalating, say solar energy investors.
“No approvals have been granted for solar energy projects for almost six months now. Only now has the government started accepting the applications. Even if they are approved now, it is difficult to commission the projects by March 2027. From April next year, it is mandatory for all new projects to have BESS, and this will push the costs up,” said one of the solar energy investors in Coimbatore.
“We had a detailed discussion with the TNERC on the BESS policy. The policy says there will be waiver of wheeling charges. The wheeling charges are applicable only if a consumer buys under open access. However, the policy says solar energy generators who store energy can sell it only to the State utility. There are many such issues with the policy that need better clarity in the policy,” says AD Thirumoorthy, State Level Renewable Energy Committee Member, Government of Tamil Nadu.
The single window approval system is functioning effectively for solar energy projects that come as a part of foreign direct investments. The others require multiple approvals, starting right from the rural local body heads. These lead to delays, pushing up the costs, he added.
While the BESS policy is a welcome move, the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation should ensure that stored solar energy is evacuated within 24 hours, so that the generator can store freshly generated energy the next day, said L. Santhosh, president of the Tamil Nadu Electricity Consumers Association.
In the last one month, some of the solar energy generators received notices demanding 8% banking charges. These are not applicable because the court has stayed the green energy open access policy of the State, he added. More sub-stations and solutions for right of way challenges to lay lines on lands belonging to various government departments are among the other issues faced by investors that threaten to slow down solar energy projects.
Published - November 22, 2026 01:12 am IST

briefs.headline: Three cyclones in three weeks: What’s happening in the Bay of Bengal? | Explained
briefs.deck: Such a frequency is uncommon but not unique this year; there were around 1.8 cyclones a year in the post-monsoon period in 1982-2022, with the average increasing after 2001
briefs.bodyText:
The story so far: Within 23 days this year, three cyclones formed over the Bay of Bengal. Of them, Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Yanam on the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28 and Murasu on November 3 near Ongole. Cyclone Akvan formed on November 16 and made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday morning (November 20, 2026).
A cyclone requires an atmospheric disturbance, abundant moisture, and favourable winds. The Bay has two main cyclone seasons, April-May and October-December. During the southwest monsoon, strong winds blowing in different directions at different altitudes suppress cyclone formation. But as the monsoon withdraws, the vertical wind shear weakens even as the waters remain warm, creating more favourable conditions.

briefs.headline: FUJIFILM’s Spectrum tour enthrals visual creators, photography enthusiasts in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: The three-day event featured specialised experience zones focusing on distinct creative mediums, including vlogging, cinematography, street photography and portraiture
briefs.bodyText:
A multi-city FUJIFILM India Spectrum Tour, bringing together of the brand’s entire range of imaging solutions from Instax cameras, digital cameras and lenses, concluded in Bengaluru recently.
The three-day event, held at the Venkatappa Art Gallery, featured specialised experience zones focusing on distinct creative mediums, including vlogging, cinematography, street photography and portraiture, attracted a large number of people.
Company executives highlighted the regional strategy behind selecting the city for this segment of the tour. "We are excited to connect with the city’s vibrant imaging community. Through Spectrum, we aim to bring our imaging heritage and cutting-edge technology closer to creators,"’ said Koji Wada, managing director of FUJIFILM India.
The tour was in Bengaluru after Gurugram and Ahmedabad, attracting local photography enthusiasts, visual creators and students who prefer to have a hands-on experience with FUJIFILM product ranges. A central component involved educational masterclasses led by established industry practitioners. Photographers including Sudhir Ramachandran and Prashant Godbole were among the participants.
Sessions covered architectural, landscape, and street photography. Other sessions led by technical experts covered niche genres such as astrophotography, wildlife documentation, and sports imaging. The event consolidated the company’s various product categories, including mirrorless camera systems, instant photography devices, and optical tools, under a unified interactive environment.
Arun Babu, associate director of the Imaging Solutions Division at FUJIFILM India, said, “In Bengaluru, through hands-on experiences, we encouraged visitors to experiment with our imaging solutions and discover new ways to express their creativity.”

stories.headline: Karnataka’s education department asks Election Commission not to deploy teachers for roll revision
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 With schools entering a crucial academic phase, the state education department has asked the chief electoral officer not to deploy govt school teachers and pre-university lecturers for any further electoral roll revision work during the remainder of the 2026-27 academic year.
In a letter dated Nov 17, additional chief secretary, department of school education and literacy, V Rashmi Mahesh urged Karnataka chief electoral officer V Anbukumar to ensure that teachers and lecturers are not assigned duties for the upcoming Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls.
The request comes after a large number of teachers and lecturers were deployed as booth-level officers and supervisors for the special intensive revision (SIR), which began in June and continued until Oct. The department had earlier said around 30% of teachers across the state had been drafted for the exercise, with Bengaluru among the worst affected.
The department pointed out that the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, prescribes a minimum of 45 working hours a week for teachers, including preparation time. Their deployment for SIR, which was extended several times and continued from June to Oct 2026, had seriously disrupted normal academic work.
The letter stated that any further deployment for the Special Summary Revision (SSR) would violate the RTE Act and severely affect curriculum completion and the conduct of examinations. It would also adversely affect students from the most vulnerable sections of society.
Govt also highlighted the academic calendar, noting that schools and colleges were conducting special classes alongside regular classes to complete the curriculum during the final quarter of the academic year.
For Class 10, three preparatory examinations are scheduled between Jan 4 and Feb 27, 2027, while the annual examinations will be held from March 22 to May 31, 2027. For II PUC, the first and second preparatory examinations are scheduled between Jan 2 and 29, 2027, followed by annual examinations from Feb 27 to May 15, 2027.
The ECI has announced the SSR of electoral rolls in Karnataka, with the claims and objections period beginning Dec 1, 2026.
The state govt has therefore also suggested issuing suitable instructions to all district election officers to ensure that teachers from govt schools and lecturers from govt PU colleges are not assigned electoral roll revision duties.
It may be recalled that the department is also planning to introduce a bill that will protect the teachers from being recruited for these duties. However, until then, teachers are likely to be deployed for a wide range of duties, including Census starting in Jan.

stories.headline: Government has asked us to reconsider restricting all protests to Freedom Park, says Bengaluru’s new Chief Commissioner of Police
stories.deck: After having taken charge during a transition phase, R. Hithendra says his first order of business is to establish a new layer of top-level governance and resolve coordination issues between commissionerates
stories.bodyText:
Following the restructuring of Bengaluru City Police into five commissionerates, several concerns, including dual reporting structures, uneven distribution of police stations, and the status of the Central Crime Branch, have been flagged.
In an interview with The Hindu, the newly-appointed Chief Commissioner of Police, Bengaluru City, R. Hithendra, addresses these concerns and explains the plans ahead.
You have taken charge during a transition phase. What will be your immediate focus?
First, to establish a new layer of top-level governance. Second, to resolve coordination issues between the commissionerates. The issue is the relocation of manpower, which we will resolve soon. Once operations begin, nobody will work in silos. Every Commissioner has to report to me, so all coordination issues will eventually come to my table. We also aim to enhance transparency in governance, make the city safer, ensure women’s safety and control drugs.
The new organisational structure has dual reporting built into it. Isn’t it problematic?
RH: This dual reporting structure is deliberate. Officers sitting in the city centre cannot supervise those posted in Kengeri or Whitefield effectively. Therefore, there will be supervision at the local level as well as at the top level.
The Traffic Commissioner will oversee planning and implementation plans, while micro-level issues will be handled by the local commissionerates. A junior officer used to head Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) and struggled to get their views across in inter-departmental meetings. Now with a Commissioner for Traffic, BTP’s point of view will be well taken. The officer will also have more time to focus on larger planning and strategy. This will help in administrative work like tenders as well.
Likewise, in the case of crimes, cases that require special attention and have pan-city repercussions will be handled by the Anti-Rowdy Squad.
There is some confusion about the future of the CCB.
There is no confusion. The CCB has been renamed the Anti-Rowdy Squad. If you go by the interpretation of statutes, only the squad has been renamed, and everything else remains unchanged.
TH: Some of the new divisions created have fewer police stations, not all urbanised police stations around the city have been added either.
RH: The idea is that the Central Commissionerate will remain the same. But the other four commissionerates will gradually expand to include more police stations of adjoining districts, where the areas are sufficiently urbanised.
TH: There has been a long-standing demand that all protests should not be restricted to Freedom Park alone. Will the The Licensing and Regulation of Protests, Demonstrations and Protest Marches (Bengaluru City) Order, 2021 be reconsidered?
RH: The Home Minister has asked us to reconsider this. We are thinking on those lines, but no decision has been made yet.
TH: Cybercrimes now account for a majority of crimes in the City. But investigations have mostly been able to crack the lowest rung and not go up further. How do you intend to change this?
RH: Skill upgradation is being undertaken for investigators at the Criminal Investigation Department. However, those who receive training are subsequently transferred. Those who are skilled need to be retained. We need to formulate a policy for this.
TH:Even in drug-related cases, arrests do not seem to go beyond the peddlers. You have till recently headed the Anti Narcotics Task Force. How do you intend to bring that experience to your new assignment?
RH: We have an FIR-to-chargesheet ratio of one is to one, which means that if there is one name in the FIR, we are chargesheeting only one person. If a peddler is caught, they must have procured the drugs from somewhere and intended to sell them to consumers. Those aspects need to be looked at. We have flagged this issue to the investigating officers. Henceforth, we will focus more on investigations following the seizure of contraband.

stories.headline: SIR: Voters challenge deletions, say officials asking them to withdraw appeals, file Form 6
stories.deck: The Hindu spoke to several people in Bengaluru who challenged their deletion, some of whom said officials had themselves submitted Form 6 applications on their behalf when they approached them seeking reversal of their deletion through an appeal
stories.bodyText:
After the final electoral rolls from the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) were published, several people whose names had been deleted challenged their exclusion. They argued that they were left out despite having completed the entire process, including attending hearings and submitting the required documents.
More than 350 appeals have been filed across Karnataka so far. The Deputy Commissioner or District Election Officer (DEO) serves as the first appellate authority in the SIR, while the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) is the second and final appellate authority if the first-stage response is unsatisfactory. According to the CEO’s office, all appeals received so far remain pending or have been disposed of at the first appellate stage.
Officials filed Form 6
The Hindu spoke to several people in Bengaluru who have challenged their deletion. While some said officials advised them to withdraw their appeals and apply afresh through Form 6, others said officials had themselves submitted Form 6 applications on their behalf when they approached them seeking reversal of their deletion through an appeal. A few of them said they had since received an Elector’s Photo Identity Card (EPIC) and were told that their names would figure in a supplementary list.
While Form 6 applications are accepted throughout the year as part of the ECI’s “continuous updation” process, this route could leave those excluded from the SIR rolls unable to vote in the upcoming local body elections, including the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) elections. The GBA elections have been directed to be conducted using the SIR final rolls by December, before even the summary revision process begins or a supplementary list is published.
Those who have appealed argue that they are not new voters seeking fresh inclusion, but people who have been voting from the same addresses and were wrongly deleted. They also questioned why they should be asked to make a declaration through Form 6 that does not reflect their circumstances, when they had already submitted documents to address the discrepancies flagged during the SIR.
Iqbal, a resident of Sarjapura, told The Hindu that he received a notice over “no mapping.” He had mapped his father’s details, whose name is on the electoral roll in Bihar,but his name was still flagged. Mr. Iqbal said that although he had shifted his residence within the city more than five years ago, his EPIC had been updated and he had submitted the required documents. His name was deleted from the final SIR rolls after figuring in the draft list.
Several people also said that while the names of all members of their families figured in the draft rolls, some were deleted from the final list. They argued that even when appeals were disposed of, the outcomes were not uniform within families.
Sahiba, a resident of Jayanagar, said she was flagged over an anomaly indicating that the age gap between two children was less than nine months. She has twins and submitted their birth certificates to establish this. However, officials subsequently raised a discrepancy in her mother’s name across records. “I explained that it was the same person and that only the spelling had changed during translation. I submitted all my documents as well as my mother’s. But I was then questioned about why I had mapped to my mother and not my father or husband. Both my father and husband are in Saudi Arabia and were not part of the 2002 rolls. Now the officials are telling me to withdraw my appeal and file Form 6,” she said.

briefs.headline: National Public School-Sarjapur Road announces closure over land dispute in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Uncertainty looms over the students of National Public School-Sarjapur Road, Carmelaram Post, after it announced closure from the next academic year.
In a circular, the school said it will be discontinuing its operations from the next academic year (2027–28), with the current academic year being its last.
The school cited an issue with its landlord as the reason. “We were repeatedly subjected to difficulties, restrictions and challenges, which made it increasingly challenging for us to carry on our operations peacefully. Despite our repeated attempts to resolve matters amicably, the situation continued to remain difficult,” the circular read.
The school said it explored the possibility of relocating the institution to other suitable premises within the surrounding vicinity. “However, finding a facility that could match our existing infrastructure, safety standards, facilities and academic requirements within such a short period proved extremely challenging. We did not want to compromise on the quality of education and the standards that our children deserve,” the circular read.
The school asked all parents to make necessary arrangements for their wards for the academic year 2027–28. 
“We knew the school was having issues with the land. But we were hoping the management would sort it out. All of us are now scrambling for admissions to other schools. That is the only discussion happening in the parents’ social media groups. While there were talks that they might accommodate the students in another sister school, there is no official communication. This is frustrating after having paid such hefty fees all these years,” said a parent.
However, when contacted, Dhananjaya Gangadharaiah, chairman, NPS Sarjapur Road, said the school has found a new location and will be shifting there soon. “We have found a new location close by. We will shift all our 350 students there and continue functioning,” he said. However, the parents have received no such information thus far.

briefs.headline: As bike taxis get green signal, commuters in Bengaluru seek safeguards
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 For many commuters, bike taxis are more than just an affordable alternative to autorickshaws. They have become an important part of daily travel, particularly for covering the last mile between the Metro station/bus stop and home. Commuters have welcomed the 
Supreme Court
’s dismissal of the state govt’s appeal against the high court order, allowing bike-taxi operations, saying the service offers a degree of affordability, accessibility and convenience other modes of transport don’t.
Fare difference is one of the biggest reasons why commuters prefer bike taxis, particularly for short-distance journeys. A ride of around 7km from a Metro station to a residential area can cost Rs 90-100 on a bike taxi, compared with more than Rs 200 by auto. Commuters also pointed to frequent auto cancellations, refusal to accept rides and demands for additional fares as other reasons they prefer bike taxis.
However, many commuters urged govt to introduce clear regulations to protect both passengers and riders. Their demands include mandatory insurance, safety norms, proper background verification of riders, transparent fares, and action against aggregators imposing steep surge pricing.
Anupama, who uses bike taxis to reach Metro stations, said: “Bike taxis offer a practical solution to Bengaluru’s mobility problems. Govt should recognise them as an important part of public transport and frame rules that protect commuters and riders. Passenger safety must be the top priority. Helmets should be compulsory for both rider and pillion, and they must be clean and properly maintained. There should also be background checks of riders, including verification of driving licences and vehicle documents.”
She also sought clear fare rules, curbs on surge pricing, and penalties for traffic violations. At the same time, she said regulations should not undermine the core purpose of bike taxis, especially their role in last-mile connectivity.
The Bike Taxi Association also welcomed the SC order, calling it a relief for thousands of people who depend on the service for livelihood. It urged govt to notify regulations at the earliest. Association president Adi Narayana M said the state should have framed rules after the high court lifted the ban instead of challenging that order in the Supreme Court. “We expect regulations covering GPS tracking, safety features and speed limits, similar to those applicable to other transport services,” he said.
Claiming that more than three lakh people work as bike-taxi riders in Bengaluru and around six lakh across Karnataka, he said the sector has the potential to generate more employment.
Following the SC order, transport minister Byrathi Suresh said Friday that instructions had already been issued to officials to frame rules for regulating bike-taxi operations.
Commuter reactions
Aiswarya Manikandan, commuter, said, “The most affordable transport option for the working class in Bengaluru is bike taxi, especially to reach bus stops or Metro stations. Autos usually cancel rides and are quite costly. If we have to depend on local autos, they charge double if they know we are from outside Bengaluru. Yes, there are some safety concerns, especially for women, and I have experienced rash driving. But I feel govt should regulate these issues and allow bike taxis.”
Dakshinya P, private firm employee appreciated the Supreme Court order. “Bike taxis are the most convenient and easily accessible mode of transport, even at night, especially if one is travelling alone. But there must be regulations as some riders can be rude. The focus should be more on ensuring customer safety.”
Shyam Padhi, engineering entrepreneur, said, the SC decision is a welcome step towards affordable and inclusive urban mobility. “As a regular bike-taxi user and resident along Whitefield’s Priority Walking Network, I believe Bengaluru’s transport challenge extends beyond Metro connectivity to the crucial last mile. Commuters need affordable, reliable options to reach Metro stations, workplaces and homes. Bike taxis also support gig-worker livelihoods and offer an alternative to expensive short-distance rides... govt should introduce clear safety, insurance, licensing and fare regulations.”
Charan, professor, added: “What Karnataka govt did was against what was really needed for commuters. I think the Supreme Court rightly applied its mind. Given Bengaluru’s traffic and the gaps in Metro connectivity, bike taxis are an important last-mile option. I commute by Metro from Whitefield to South End Circle and from the Metro to college. An auto from South End to Christ (university) would cost me Rs 100-120, while a bike taxi usually costs Rs 60-75. But it is not just about cost. Bike taxis give you predictability in that last-mile journey as cancellations are very rare.”
Waseem Akram K, IT professional said asa regular bike-taxi user, he finds them cheaper, quicker and extremely useful during peak hours. “When bike taxis were banned, I struggled to get autos, and drivers would sometimes ask for Rs 20, Rs 30 or even Rs 50 extra to accept a ride. There were also instances where they would refuse to drop me at the pinned destination. For a city like Bengaluru, where traffic is already a major problem, bike taxis are an economical and convenient option and should be allowed to operate,” he said.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru man escapes shooting attempt after snatching pistol from daughter's 'lover'
briefs.deck: Two men have been identified in a shooting attempt at a cloth merchant in Bengaluru's Puttenahalli area. The suspects, Syed Amin and Afan, were angry after a failed romantic relationship. Amin's father had promised to keep him away from the girl, Umme Iman, whose father advised against the relationship. briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Police are searching for two men who allegedly attempted to shoot at a girl's father with a pistol in Vinayakanagar, in south Bengaluru's Puttenahalli area, on Friday night.
The suspects have been identified as Syed Amin and Afan, police said.
According to police, Amin was in a relationship with Umme Iman, daughter of cloth merchant Azmat Pasha.
When Iman did not wish to marry him, Pasha advised Amin to stay away from her. Amin's father had also promised Pasha that he would keep his son away from Iman.
Angered by this, Amin and his associate Afan allegedly barged into Pasha's shop. During a heated argument, Afan tried to shoot at Pasha but failed after Pasha managed to pull the pistol away, police said.
Police are searching for both suspects.

briefs.headline: Report documents impact of restrictions on the right to protest in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: The report by PUCL-Karnataka highlights how the restriction has rendered protests invisible to the public and has had cascading impact on those who seek State accountability
briefs.bodyText:
A study on the impact of confining protests to Freedom Park observes that the 2021 Licensing Order restricting protests in Bengaluru to Freedom Park has effectively turned a constitutionally guaranteed right into a permission-based activity, shrinking the space for public dissent and leaving a cascading impact on people who seek State accountability.
The report by PUCL-Karnataka and published by the Campaign for the Right to Protest, after interviews with activists, trade unionists, lawyers and community leaders over three years, was released by Justice (Retd.) H. N. Nagamohan Das at a public meeting held in the city.
Lack of visibility
The report highlights how the restriction has rendered protests invisible to the public.
While Freedom Park is centrally located in the city, “it is an area which is completely invisible to the city’s people,” notes the report, which adds that, in the past, protests took place in areas located at crowded junctions, spaces that are frequented by pedestrians or visible to authorities they wanted to address.
These included places in front of the offices of authorities the protesters wanted to address or areas such as M.G. Road Gandhi Statute, Maurya Circle, Mysore Bank Circle, Town Hall, Maurya Circle and Cubbon Park.
The report also notes that different protests taking place simultaneously at Freedom Park dilute the efforts of civil society groups to make their voices heard.
‘Arbitrary and unlawful response’
According to the report, while the Licensing Order has not stopped people in Bengaluru from protesting outside the designated area, it has empowered the police to respond in “arbitrary and unlawful” manner.
“It has been an increasingly common sight since the restriction of protests to Freedom Park, to see Bengaluru Police forcefully detaining protestors, at times violently. In many cases, they have also registered FIRs,” it reads.
The report cites several instances such as the lathi charging and detention of around 200 Dalit activists who had gathered in December 2022 to demand the implementation of internal reservation within the Scheduled Caste category, detention of left party protestors in October 2023 at Freedom Park during a protest against the Israel-led attack on Palestine, arrest of 71 farmers on 15 August 2022 for planning a protest in Devanahalli against forced land acquisition, among others. It notes that protests against Kogilu slum demolition, a protest by ward attenders of Victoria Hospital and general strike demanding repeal of labour codes also faced similar ‘police highhandedness.’
It further observes that protests organised by working class groups are met with force and detention, and when middle-class residents raise civic issues, the police are less likely to behave violently.
Creative ways
The report also observes how groups have resorted to creative ways to bypass restrictions on assemblies. Cases in point include the Domestic Workers’ Rights Union gathering in front of the Labour Commissioner’s office with copies of letters responding to the draft Karnataka Domestic Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Bill 2025, and ‘My Vote, My Right’ coalition working on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) issue gathering in front of the Chief Electoral Officer’s office with questions printed on placards.
The report also discusses the cascading effect of the restriction order. "The Licensing Order was issued to regulate protests. The police have invoked it against reading circles, film screenings, pamphleteering, signature campaigns in the Metro, and meetings in private venues," it notes.
“Organisers must now provide the Aadhaar cards of five people, and the police collect the addresses of participants. Intelligence officials follow and sit with organisers, and 90 police personnel photograph and film those who attend. This is a burden on privacy and on the freedom to associate without being identified and recorded,” it adds.

briefs.headline: Karnataka Chief Minister to lead delegation to Japan for investment talks, urban-planning study
briefs.deck: The visit will focus on two areas: attracting fresh investments from Japanese companies and understanding Japan’s approach to urban planning, transport, waste management and infrastructure development
briefs.bodyText:
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar will lead a high-level Karnataka government delegation to Japan from Monday to Wednesday (November 23 to 25) to explore investment opportunities and study the country’s urban development models for possible adoption in Bengaluru and other cities in the State.
The delegation will visit Nagoya on Monday (November 23), Osaka on Tuesday (November 24) and Tokyo on Wednesday (November 25). The visit will focus on two areas: attracting fresh investments from Japanese companies and understanding Japan’s approach to urban planning, transport, waste management and infrastructure development.
Large and Medium Industries and Infrastructure Development Minister M.B. Patil will accompany the Chief Minister and lead the industrial engagements. He will also head the State’s investment promotion efforts in Japan and South Korea.
Meetings with Japanese companies
According to an official statement, the Chief Minister and the Commerce and Industries Department officials would hold meetings with senior representatives of leading Japanese companies to discuss their investment plans and showcase opportunities in Karnataka.
The discussions would cover sectors such as automobiles and electric vehicle components, speciality chemicals, advanced materials, pharmaceuticals, industrial automation, and manufacturing.
The companies include Toyota and Panasonic Automotive Systems in the automobile and EV components sector, Mitsubishi Chemical Group, Takeda Pharmaceuticals, Yokogawa Electric and Sumitomo Corporation.
The State delegation will present Karnataka’s industrial policies and incentives, including its aerospace and defence policy, additional capital subsidy of up to 20% for investments in backward and priority taluks, the KIADB Digital Industrial Land Bank and the single-window clearance system.
The delegation will also meet the Executive vice-president of the Japan External Trade Organisation to discuss ways to strengthen institutional support for Japanese companies looking to invest in the State.
The companies will be invited to the Global Investors Meet-2027, organised by Invest Karnataka, which will be held at the Bengaluru Palace from April 20 to 22.
Study of Japan’s urban planning
The delegation, along with officials of the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), will study Japan’s urban development practices, particularly in waste management, waste-to-energy, urban planning, public transport and transit planning, architecture and urban design.
Tokyo and Osaka have been selected for their experience in managing large urban populations and developing integrated infrastructure. Tokyo is known for its integrated transport network and redevelopment around railway stations, while Osaka offers examples of large-scale urban renewal and metropolitan planning.
As part of the visit, the delegation will visit Tokyo Midtown Roppongi along with representatives of Nikken Sekkei, a leading Japanese architecture and urban design firm, the statement said.
The mixed-use development will be studied for its approach to urban redevelopment, transit-oriented development, land readjustment, mixed land use and the management of green spaces. These are among the areas considered relevant to Bengaluru’s urban expansion.
The delegation will also meet senior management of JFE Engineering Corporation at its Tokyo headquarters to understand the company’s work in waste management, waste-to-energy projects and urban infrastructure.
The delegation will include GBA Chief Commissioner M. Maheshwar Rao, Commerce and Industries Department Principal Secretary S. Selvakumar, Commissioner for Industrial Development and Invest Karnataka Forum CEO Khushboo Goel Chowdhary, besides officials from the Chief Minister’s Office, GBA and the Industries Department.
Industry meetings with Japanese companies are scheduled to continue until November 27, the statement added.

briefs.headline: Warner Music Group to develop Bengaluru as global technology hub
briefs.deck: The New-York based company is keen to leverage the city’s engineering and product talent to develop business-critical systems spanning music distribution, data infrastructure and predictive AI
briefs.bodyText:
New York-based Warner Music Group (WMG), one of the world’s big three global music companies alongside Universal Music Group and Sony Music, is positioning Bengaluru as one of its principal global technology centres, leveraging the city’s engineering and product talent to develop business-critical systems spanning music distribution, data infrastructure and predictive artificial intelligence (AI).
Leho Nigul, global chief technology officer, WMG, told The Hindu that the company already has more than 45 engineers and product leaders at its Bengaluru facility, with recruitment under way to expand its capabilities across backend platform engineering, enterprise data architecture, machine learning, and engineering and product leadership.
Tech platforms
“The Bengaluru centre is developing technology platforms that support WMG’s global operations, including backend data infrastructure, audience insight engines and proprietary marketing products that are deployed across international markets,” he said, adding that the work also covered enterprise data pipelines and systems supporting music distribution.
Describing Bengaluru as a core pillar of the company’s technology strategy, Mr. Nigul said the investment reflected a multi-year commitment to building one of WMG’s primary global engineering centres. While the company has not disclosed its long-term headcount targets, it expects the facility’s role to expand significantly.
According to him, the music company is also looking to strengthen the connection between its technology operations and its existing creative and commercial presence in India. Over the next three years, its priorities will include scaling engineering capabilities, expanding local leadership and integrating the Bengaluru team more closely with its wider India operations.
Deploying AI
WMG is also deploying AI and machine learning in rights management, particularly to improve royalty processing and ensure accurate compensation for songwriters across international markets, its global CTO said.
The company is automating the ingestion of rights data and royalty processing to accelerate payout cycles and improve reporting accuracy across digital platforms. It is also using solutions such as ‘Sureel AI’, which it recently acquired, to strengthen the attribution of music and ensure creators receive appropriate recognition across digital services.
The focus on technology assumes added significance as the company seeks to improve the tracking of music rights and royalty payments in an increasingly fragmented digital distribution environment.
Mr. Nigul said Bengaluru’s availability of engineering and product talent, particularly in high-throughput architectures, scalable data infrastructure and AI, was a key factor behind the company’s long-term commitment to the region.
Although WMG has not disclosed specific investment figures for India over the next three years, it sees Bengaluru emerging as one of its largest and most critical technology hubs globally.

stories.headline: Gold falls 4.49%, silver 6.6% in a single day; wedding shoppers get buying chance

stories.bodyText:
Gold and silver prices saw a steep decline on Friday, falling by as much as 6.6% as a firm US dollar, high bond yields and expectations of tighter monetary policy by the US Federal Reserve dampened investor sentiment.
On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), gold futures dropped as much as 4.49%, or Rs 5,733, to Rs 1,21,719 per 10 grams from the previous close of Rs 1,27,452 per 10 grams. Silver futures faced even heavier selling, declining 6.6%, or Rs 10,416, to Rs 1,47,066 per kg.
The sharp correction in the two precious metals also affected gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Nippon India ETF Gold BeES, ICICI Prudential Gold ETF and Quantum Gold ETF were among the funds that lost up to 5%, touching their respective 52-week lows during the session. Silver ETFs also came under significant pressure. Nippon India Silver ETF, ICICI Prudential Silver ETF and Mirae Asset Silver ETF were among those that declined by as much as 6%, hitting fresh 52-week lows.
Gold Price Crash Brings Cheer To Wedding Households 
But, for households that had postponed jewellery purchases because of elevated prices, the correction offers an opportunity to reassess their budgets and bring forward planned purchases!
Cheaper gold can substantially reduce the overall cost of jewellery, particularly for buyers planning to purchase heavier bridal sets, necklaces and bangles. 
While some consumers are waiting to see whether prices decline further, others have begun placing orders to take advantage of the lower rates.
At EKARAA Jewellery, the fall in precious metal prices has prompted different reactions among customers. Mehul Jain, the company's founder, told ET that the savings were less significant for smaller ornaments but became more substantial for expensive, heavier pieces.
“While smaller jewellery pieces have not seen a significant impact on overall budgets, the difference is more noticeable in heavier, high-value pieces, where even a slight change in metal prices can translate into considerable savings,” he was quoted as saying.
Jain said some buyers were holding off on purchases in the hope of a further decline in prices. Others, however, were using the opportunity to select designs, discuss customisation requirements and plan wedding-related orders. The response indicates that changing 
gold prices
 are affecting not only the timing of jewellery purchases but also the way customers plan them.
Zen Diamond India has also seen the benefit of softer gold prices, which have added momentum to an already strong sales trend. “Lower gold prices are certainly an incentive for consumers to advance their purchases, particularly with the wedding season approaching,” said Neil Sonawala, managing director of Zen Diamond India. “We expect this to translate into stronger demand in the coming weeks, especially among customers who have already planned their jewellery purchases.”
Yash Kataria, CEO of Kataria Jewellers, said the price decline had offered welcome relief to families preparing for weddings in the coming months. Even a modest reduction can make a difference when households need to purchase multiple jewellery pieces for the bride and other family members.
According to Kataria, customers who had delayed buying in anticipation of lower prices were now reconsidering their plans. He suggested that families with weddings approaching should make purchases based on their actual requirements and budgets instead of waiting indefinitely for another price correction.
Meanwhile, minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October meeting, released on Wednesday, indicated that nearly all policymakers believed interest rates would need to rise further to bring inflation under control.
The prospect of tighter monetary policy has pushed bond yields higher and strengthened the US dollar, reducing the appeal of gold and silver to investors. Forced selling across financial markets has added to the downward pressure on the two metals.

stories.headline: IndusInd Bank terminates Sumant Kathpalia’s services, invokes clawback provisions
stories.deck: The bank’s board acted on an inquiry report by a former Bombay High Court judge and invoked malus and clawback provisions from March 24, 2020
stories.bodyText:
IndusInd Bank has terminated the services of its former Managing Director and CEO Sumant Kathpalia with immediate effect following disciplinary proceedings against him.
The bank’s board, acting as the disciplinary authority, took the decision at its meeting on November 20, 2026, based on the findings of an inquiry report submitted by a former Bombay High Court judge on November 18, 2026.
The bank also decided to invoke applicable malus and clawback provisions with effect from March 24, 2020, the date of Mr. Kathpalia’s initial appointment as MD and CEO.
In a regulatory filing, the bank said the action was in continuation of its earlier disclosures dated April 29 and May 21, 2025, and disclosures in its annual reports for the financial years 2024-25 and 2025-26.
Mr. Kathpalia and Deputy CEO Arun Khurana resigned from the bank on April 29, 2025, with effect from the same day, following which the board appointed a Committee of Executives to oversee the operations of the bank till a new MD and CEO assumed charge or for a period of three months.
The bank’s board took note of his resignation as MD and CEO and as a director, but did not communicate that he would continue to remain in the bank’s employment until further intimation.
Subsequently, disciplinary proceedings were initiated against him under the bank’s internal code of conduct, and he was placed under suspension with effect from June 18, 2025, pending completion of the proceedings. The latest decision follows the submission of the inquiry report and the board’s consideration of its findings.
In May 2025, the board had suspected the involvement of certain employees in the derivatives, microfinance and balance sheet “fraud” and directed the bank to report the matter to investigative agencies and regulatory authorities.
The bank has appropriately accounted for and reflected the impact of all discrepancies identified in these reports while finalising the financial results for the quarter and twelve months ended March 2025.
In March 2025, the private sector bank had reported accounting lapses in the derivative portfolio, which were estimated to have an adverse impact of approximately 2.35% of the bank’s net worth as of December 2024.
Following this, the bank appointed external agency PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) to assess the impact on the bank’s balance sheet and lapses at various levels, and to suggest remedial action. The agency, in its report, quantified the negative impact as of June 30, 2024, at ₹1,979 crore.

“Our goal is to double India’s plastics exports in volume over the next four years through innovation, advanced technology, new markets and sustainable manufacturing. PLEXCONNECT 2026 has set the direction, and I am confident the best years for Indian plastics exports lie ahead,” he emphasised.
Highlighting the road ahead, Sribash Dasmohapatra, Executive Director, PLEXCONCIL, said, “The potential of India’s plastics exports is tremendous. As new Free Trade Agreements are opening doors, Africa and Latin America are emerging as high-growth destinations.”
He said Indian manufacturers are now investing in advanced materials and smart technology like never before.
“With our FTA booklet and the insights from PLEXCONNECT 2026, PLEXCONCIL is determined to help every exporter, especially our MSMEs, turn that potential into real export orders, new buyers and lasting growth in global markets,” he stated.
The entire plastics ecosystem came together under one roof as manufacturers, technocrats, policy makers, diplomats, government officials and bankers deliberated about the challenges and opportunities.
Across six panel discussions, the conference covered everything an exporter needs to grow.
The sessions looked at expanding India’s plastics footprint from Maharashtra to Africa, using FTAs to move from market access to market success, next-generation polymers and advanced materials, the role of AI in manufacturing, future-ready trade finance, and building supply chains that can stand up to global shocks.
