stories.headline: India, Canada push for wider market access as 6th round of trade talks ends
stories.deck: India and Canada concluded the sixth round of CEPA negotiations in New Delhi after a series of discussions. The negotiations focused on vital areas like trade in goods, services, and investment promotion. Both sides aim for a balanced agreement that benefits farmers, businesses, and MSMEs in both countries. Commerce secretaries from both nations reviewed the progress made during this round.
stories.bodyText:
India and Canada have wrapped up the sixth round of negotiations for their proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), with both sides pushing for an ambitious and balanced trade pact to expand market access, boost investments and strengthen economic ties. The talks, held in New Delhi from November 11 to 20, concluded on Friday, with progress reported across key areas of trade and investment.
According to a release issued by the ministry of commerce and industry, the latest round covered several areas, including trade in goods and services, rules of origin, trade remedies, intellectual property and investment promotion.
Towards the conclusion of the negotiations, commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal met Canada's vice minister of International Trade Glenn Purves and his delegation in New Delhi. They reviewed the progress made during the sixth round and assessed the overall status of the CEPA discussions.
Both sides reiterated their commitment to concluding an agreement that is ambitious, balanced and commercially meaningful. They also stressed the need to ensure tangible benefits for farmers, industries, businesses and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in both countries.
The proposed pact is expected to open up additional opportunities for trade and investment. 
It also aims to strengthen resilient and diversified supply chains between the two countries.
The sixth round began with a meeting between Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal and Canada's minister of international trade Maninder Sidhu in New Delhi on November 11.
Both ministers emphasised the need for a balanced and mutually beneficial agreement. They said it should provide meaningful market access, build on the complementary strengths of the two economies and create fresh opportunities for trade and investment.
The ministers also reviewed the progress of negotiations and guided their respective teams to advance discussions constructively, the ministry said.
The Indian negotiating team was led by chief negotiator Brij Mohan Mishra, while the Canadian side was headed by chief negotiator Mary-Catherine Speirs.
The ministry said substantive discussions took place across various negotiating tracks during the latest round, with both sides making progress towards advancing the proposed agreement.
The negotiations are guided by the shared objective of concluding the pact within the ambitious timelines envisaged by the leaders of both countries, the release added.
The conclusion of the sixth round reflects the continued engagement and commitment of India and Canada to take the negotiations forward and strengthen their bilateral economic and commercial relationship, the ministry said.

briefs.headline: Hafele targets 50% localisation in India, eyes sustained double-digit growth
briefs.deck: The premium German home and kitchen solution brand plans to broaden its living solutions portfolio and strengthen its presence across India’s home interiors market says Hafele South Asia MD Frank Schloeder.
briefs.bodyText:
Hafele India said it has made significant progress in strengthening its local sourcing and manufacturing capabilities, increasing localisation from around 10% to over 30% currently.
The premium home interiors solutions company now aims to take this contribution to approximately 50% over the next few years, as it is looking at a broader localisation strategy, supported by a growing network of suppliers and an expanding manufacturing footprint in India, Frank Schloeder, Managing Director, Hafele South Asia said in an interview.
“Localisation remains a key priority. The company’s focus is now on developing a stronger and more integrated supplier ecosystem within India, while progressively expanding domestic manufacturing capabilities,” he said.
This progress enables Hafele to bring together German quality standards, local expertise and a deeper understanding of the Indian market. Its manufacturing facility in Maharashtra is also part of its established manufacturing presence in the country. The company is on the process of setting up a larger manufacturing unit with an investment of ₹200 crore up aid localisation.
This also reflects its commitment to the ‘Make in India’ initiative, while continuing to maintain the quality and standards associated with its premium product portfolio.
Alongside this, Hafele is targeting sustained double-digit growth over the coming decade, with the ambition of potentially scaling its India business three to four times over this period, he said.
With a revenue of approximately Rs. 1,200 crore in India in 2025, Hafele’s long-term ambitions are growing scope of the home interiors market and its established presence across the country.
The company currently has a footprint of roughly 15,000 outlets, including its own stores, franchisees and multi-brand outlets and this distribution network is set to grow.
Looking ahead, the company’s growth strategy is focused on building on this existing presence and continuing to expand its business over the next decade, the MD said.
Over the years, Hafele has evolved from a specialist in furniture fittings and hardware into a provider of comprehensive home interior solutions. With kitchens at the core of its business, the company has progressively expanded into wardrobes, bedrooms and other areas of the home.
Its portfolio today extends across kitchen accessories, appliances, refrigerators, ovens, microwaves, lighting, coffee machines and surfaces, bringing together the various components required to create a complete kitchen, wardrobe or home interior.
“This expansion from individual fittings to the entire room, and eventually to the broader home interior, has been central to our growth over the years,” he said.
Beyond its own growth, Hafele sees considerable potential for India to strengthen the country’s furniture manufacturing capabilities.
Mr Schloeder called upon the government to develop and implement a robust strategy to turn India into a significant furniture manufacturing and exports hub. This would significantly benefit a large number of MSMEs he stated.
“The furniture sector presents an opportunity to scale domestic production, reduce dependence on imports and generate employment, supported by greater industry collaboration and government engagement,” he said.
Having completed 23 years in India, the country remains an important market for the company, among top three globally, as it looks to strengthen its local capabilities while continuing to expand its reach.
The company is currently participating in ACETECH 2026 showcasing it’s innovations across kitchens, wardrobes, appliances, lighting and surfaces.

briefs.headline: Lam Research intensifies focus on Indian semiconductor mart as local fab discussions gather momentum
briefs.deck: Despite India’s large pool of mechanical, electrical, chemical and software engineering graduates, the semiconductor industry faces a shortage of people with practical knowledge of fabrication processes, says Lam Research India head Rangesh Raghavan
briefs.bodyText:
Lam Research, a California-based company that builds wafer-fabrication equipment and services used in semiconductor manufacturing, is currently in active discussions with Tata Group and other emerging players to supply equipment for their upcoming fabs, marking the start of Lam’s local commercial revenue in India, Rangesh Raghavan, Corporate Vice President & Managing Director, Lam Research India, told The Hindu.
Although Lam has been present in Bengaluru for 25 years, it has so far operated primarily as a technology and engineering centre, without domestic semiconductor manufacturing customers. This is expected to change as India’s semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem takes shape. Its workforce has grown manifold over the last seven to eight years, although the company does not disclose employee numbers.
The Bengaluru centre has evolved from a small software development and back-office operation into a product engineering and development hub contributing to virtually every product in Lam’s global portfolio. Its engineers work on advanced technologies supporting semiconductor manufacturing processes at two-nanometre and below levels. The facility also houses a specialised engineering laboratory comparable to the company’s global R&D facilities in the US.
Indian engineers develop critical subsystems used in fabrication equipment, including radio-frequency systems, temperature control, fluid delivery, gas and chemical handling, and robotics. Product development is distributed across five to six laboratories globally, with teams working on individual components before integrating them into complete systems.
Lam is also seeking to expand its engagement with Indian suppliers as it diversifies its global supply chain. Pandemic-related disruptions exposed vulnerabilities in semiconductor supply networks, prompting manufacturers to identify alternative sources. The company is developing domestic capabilities in precision metal machining, printed circuit board assemblies and cable assemblies, leveraging engineering expertise available in India’s automotive, aerospace and medical equipment sectors.
Lam’s proposed wholly owned manufacturing facility in India will produce silicon components. It has announced investments of around ₹ 10,000 crore towards silicon component manufacturing and expanding its R&D capabilities. The facility will have specialised technology for growing large 450 mm silicon ingots (bars or blocks).
According to Mr. Raghavan, workforce development is a significant challenge, given the limited availability of specialised expertise in India. “Despite India’s large pool of mechanical, electrical, chemical and software engineering graduates, the semiconductor industry faces a shortage of people with practical knowledge of fabrication processes,’’ he commented.
One initiative addressing this gap is Semiverse, Lam’s virtual semiconductor fabrication training platform, developed with the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) and the Indian Institute of Science (IISc). Announced as a strategic India-U.S. initiative in 2023, it uses a digital twin of a fabrication facility to simulate manufacturing processes and experiments. Semiconductor manufacturers globally also use the platform to model processes before undertaking expensive physical experiments.
The programme addresses the high capital costs of establishing physical fabrication laboratories, which restrict practical semiconductor training to a handful of Indian institutions. Semiverse provides qualifying universities access to virtual fabrication environments without requiring investments in expensive infrastructure.
Lam estimates the annual value of the platform and associated services provided free to eligible Indian universities at around $29 million. More than 110 institutions have enrolled, and approximately 4,000 students have graduated. The company expects to train over 60,000 students during the 10 years beginning 2025. ISM and IISc determine eligibility, based on whether institutions offer semiconductor-related courses.
Mr. Raghavan said, skilling efforts would also extend to technicians and shop-floor workers. Through an NGO partnership, Lam is funding a 240-hour electronics assembly training programme for underprivileged students with high-school qualifications. The first batch comprises 300 students, while 82 of 90 participants in the pilot batch have secured placements.
For its silicon components facility, Lam is exploring specialised training with the government in areas such as single-crystal silicon production. Mr. Raghavan said developing the workforce would require classroom instruction followed by practical, on-the-job exposure.
“India’s semiconductor opportunity will depend on building capabilities across equipment, materials, components, suppliers and skilled manpower, rather than focusing only on attracting fabrication plants,’’ he added.
Growing demand from artificial intelligence and data-centre infrastructure was creating opportunities for new manufacturing locations, he said, but added that high capital requirements, technological complexity and long investment cycles made rapid outcomes unlikely.

briefs.headline: Gold, copper, aluminium dive to at least 7-month lows
briefs.deck: Hawkish commentary from U.S. Fed and concerns over global economic growth have been among the more prominent concerns.
briefs.bodyText:
Prices of prominent metals including gold, copper and aluminium tumbled to at least seven-month lows on hawkish commentary about U.S. Fed seeking to increase rates and weighing concerns over global economic growth in the immediate term.
Benchmark price of the yellow metal, that is, at the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) slipped to their lowest since September 2025 to close this week at $3,521.38 per troy ounce.
Further, benchmark price of copper – that is, at the London Metal Exchange (LME) – slipped to their lowest in about eight months at $12,230.40 per metric tonne.
Reference price for aluminium at LME also slipped to an almost one-year low at $2,824.5 per metric tonne.
Gold nosedives
Gold prices in 2026 have taken a nosedive from where they began the year, with the yellow metal falling over 25% from its peak, with a majority of the unwinding taking place over the last couple of months. Gold has seen exponential growth since 2022, rising 145% globally till now, with prices hitting multiple record highs last year.
Harshal Barot, principal consultant at Metals Focus Limited, says the primary driver of the downswing in gold prices is the change in global macroeconomic conditions.
“The biggest driver (in price movements) is that the macro story changed. Since the (Iran-U.S.) war, inflation expectations, energy prices, and anticipation of interest rate hikes capped gains for the metal.”
With traders expecting a more hawkish stance from the U.S. Federal Reserve, the U.S. dollar has also gained strength in recent weeks. It is important to note that gold typically thrives in a weak-dollar environment.
U.S. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller’s remarks last week further cemented expectations of a rate hike next month.
According to the FedWatch tool, traders see a 95% probability of the Fed hiking interest rates by a quarter percentage point next month, taking the target range to 4.00–4.25%.
Further, rising US Treasury yields have also added pressure on gold prices. Since gold is a non-interest-bearing asset, higher Treasury yields increase the opportunity cost of holding the precious metal, making yield-bearing assets relatively more attractive.
Gold analysts expect the metal to trade range-bound over the next couple of quarters and into the beginning of FY28. The precious metal is expected to trade between $3,200 and $3,800 in the near term.
Copper, aluminium slump
In September, copper prices had rallied to record-highs as purchasers in United States rushed to stock up the metal anticipating President Donald Trump would impose steep tariffs on the import of refined copper.
This apprehension compounded with the fact that the global economy was already mired amidst lower copper production in the first half of the calendar year.
However, since then, hawkish commentary from U.S. Fed and expectations of decline in demand from industries, especially from China and the global technology industry.
The apprehension about lowered demand for copper particularly originates from the world of artificial intelligence and about continued massive investments in the realm following the Nvidia fallout.
According to the industry body Federation of Indian Mineral Industries (FIMI), the correction in prices of both aluminium and copper is also due to purchasers having already booked profits from the erstwhile price rally and easing supply concerns.
“In aluminium, expectations of increased production from Indonesia have also put pressure on prices, while copper prices have been affected by concerns over industrial demand and short-term market sentiment,” they observed.
However, according to them, copper prices would remain firm over the longer-term owing limited growth in mine supply, declining ore grades and rising demand from electrification, renewable energy and power infrastructure.
Further, aluminium demand would benefit from scaling infrastructure, electric vehicles and renewable energy sectors, though, they state, “New capacity in Indonesia and the recovery of Middle Eastern smelters may limit price increases.”

briefs.headline: India a swing vote at IMO meeting on shipping decarbonisation
briefs.bodyText:
In 2025 October, the U.S. disrupted the International Maritime Organization (IMO) meeting convened to vote on decarbonisation of global shipping, threatening retaliation and sanctions such as vessels being blocked from U.S. ports. That April, a simple majority at the relevant IMO committee had formulated a framework to move ahead on net zero but the U.S., leveraging reservations among fossil fuel producers such as Saudi Arabia, forced a postponement of the vote by a year.
This year, meetings have been scheduled at the IMO in London from November 23, with a vote expected on December 4. India had voted in favour of the adjournment last year and is now seen as a swing state with stakeholders seeking its active intervention for moving ahead on net zero. India has not yet decided its position for the vote, official sources say; much would depend on the preparatory meetings that would flesh out technical and financial details.
Principle of climate justice
India’s position would nevertheless be broadly in line with the principle of climate justice articulated by concepts such as the CBDR-RC, Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities, as well as its national interest as an importer of fossil fuels that would benefit from a turn away from them if alternatives were available and affordable. “India’s position in climate change mitigation negotiations has always been based on CBDR-RC, advocating climate justice and just transition. Who pays for the transition and who gets supported in the transition are key questions for India,” says Cmde Debesh Lahiri, advisor at the National Centre of Excellence in Green Ports and Shipping (NCoEGPS), a co-action centre between the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) and The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI).
In 2023, the IMO had committed to net zero by 2050, enthusiastically supported by the then U.S. government (Joe Biden). In April 2025, the relevant IMO committee had proposed a framework that would cut the greenhouse gas intensity of each ship in a timebound manner, collect a carbon tax from non-compliant ships, reward performers, and administer a fund to support alternatives. A 43% reduction for every ship by 2035 was targeted. Compliance deficits were to be paid for in part by paying into the IMO administered fund. But the effort was upended largely by the U.S.
This year, however, the U.S. has made a submission at the IMO indicating it is ready to work within IMO structures and procedures but staying firm on key issues. It is against an IMO-administered fund, any carbon price, and unilateral regional mechanisms such as the EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime. It decries alternative fuels, such as green ammonia and green methanol without quite naming them, as unproven and expensive. It has sought to protect traditional bunker fuels and advocated Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) and biofuels in which it has a market interest as a potential supplier.
The EU too has softened its position a bit on fuel intensity and indicated easier targets but is firm on the ultimate goal of net zero. Canada, Australia, the UK and South Africa have made a joint submission updating the April 2025 framework. Japan and Brazil have advocated a softer start.
India would likely oppose a blanket and equal carbon tax on every ship, says Mr. Lahiri. India is concerned about the availability, affordability and scalability of alternative green fuels on a global basis and will prefer a preparatory phase to ensure that the arrangements are commercially feasible. “An imposition of a financial levy should make a reference to the concept of who is principally responsible for climate change,” says Mr. Lahiri.
What would muddle the picture, however, is that ship ownership is often opaque with flags of convenience such as Guinea-Bissau, Liberia and Marshall Islands accounting for much tonnage. Classifications such as developed and developing don’t always apply in such cases.
Nevertheless, India could see an opportunity in biofuels. India’s embrace of ethanol in road transportation is largely driven by considerations of saving foreign exchange and investing the money in the domestic economy. India also has an active green fuel programme, with several green ammonia projects on the drawing board with assured offtake agreements, although much work remains before investment starts pouring in. India could leverage its closeness to Singapore, a major bunkering point, to become a supplier of green fuels to global shipping. Any support that could make India a green fuel maker would be welcome.

briefs.headline: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
briefs.deck: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said
briefs.bodyText:
“India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.
"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI.
The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.
"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.
The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.
Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.
The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.
"What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.
"There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.
Bilateral trade in goods and services between India and Finland stood at around $3.7 billion in 2025-26, marking a growth of about 25% over the previous year, and a 38.5% rise from $2.64 billion in 2021-22.
The startup event, Polar Bear Pitching, originated in Oulu, northern Finland, and has expanded internationally, connecting startups with investors and business networks.
Six startups pitched their ideas on Friday at the third India edition of Polar Bear Pitching, with Mumbai-based Yash Goliya of Suryudey Plastic Electronics Private Limited emerging as the winner.
Mr. Goliya will now compete alongside founders from other countries at the global event in Finland in February 2027. "I'm gonna make India proud and get the trophy home," Mr. Goliya said after his win.
Last year's India edition winner, Anshul Patyal, who represented computing hardware startup Vicharak, secured third place at the global competition in February this year.
The winner of the main Polar Bear Pitching competition in Oulu receives a cash prize of 10,000 euros (around ₹10.1 lakh).

stories.headline: Rishabh Pant: Down but never out
stories.deck: Rishabh Pant has endured a turbulent year, losing his Test vice-captaincy and his place in the ODIs, but his response remains unmistakably his own. In Wellington, he turned a cautious start into an audacious century, completing the SENA set and silencing critics, if only temporarily. Through the noise, scrutiny and setbacks, Pant continues to entertain, defy convention and remind everyone why he…
stories.bodyText:
Wellington:
 The last 12 months have been a wild ride for 
Rishabh Pant
 in international cricket. From losing his Test vice-captaincy to getting axed from the ODI squad, the wicketkeeper-batter experienced one of the lowest phases of his career. Just like his bottom hand coming off the bat while going big, Pant was losing his grip on his cricket. It's never easy for any cricketer to maintain Pant-like standards in the toughest format, and here was Pant, hoping to do something only he could conceive.
Turbulence has largely remained the undertone whenever he has stepped onto the cricket field. Even off the field, the chatter and noise continue to put him on a constant trial, where his indecision at the MCG and Guwahati overshadows eight-plus years of consistency.
Usual drama preceded his arrival in New Zealand for the Test series preparations. An injury during the Irani Cup meant he wasn't supposed to get ideal game time, like most of his teammates. However, he landed, shook off the jet lag and was back doing Pant things, this time even better.
Even without intention, Pant ends up playing for the gallery. It's a wild ride best enjoyed with a box full of hot chips, and he didn't disappoint the spectators soaking in the sun on the grass banks. 
Initially, during his 100-run partnership with Shubman Gill, Pant was losing balance, struggling for shape and didn't quite middle the ball as well as he would have liked.
Then came the loud shout from the middle, where he asked for a bat change, and Mohammed Siraj knew exactly which piece of willow to fetch from the kit bag. The move worked as he hit Jacob Duffy for back-to-back sixes, found a boundary and struck the "Pantastic" note he was struggling to find. Captain Gill became a mere spectator when the fireworks were underway from the other end.
A relieved Rishabh Pant after scoring his century. (BCCI | X)
The half-century was up, and the waltz from 15 to 50 runs received a loud roar from the spectators. The left-hander scored just 15 off the first 37 deliveries he faced but scored his next 37 runs in just 18 deliveries. Gill, meanwhile, could only move from 91 to 98. The initial measured start soon transformed into fluency, and Pant now held the key to India's strength and their grip on the contest.
The morning of Day 4 was going to be crucial, and the roles reversed briefly when Anshul Kamboj took over the scoring intensity from Pant. But when he got back on strike and got his eye in, boundaries began to flow from both ends, and the left-hander was into the 90s. It seemed like a matter of two shots, but Pant wasn't going to throw it away in search of the glory shot. It seemed he badly wanted the magic number, even if it meant waiting 15 deliveries before creating history.
At 99, there was palpable tension in the stands because there was a strong anticipation of something wild waiting to happen. A few phones were out, and Pant got the glory hit, ensuring a strong connection to clear the ropes. Out came the helmet, followed by a look to the heavens. There were no wild punches or somersaults, just a gentle raise of the bat, soaking in the applause and feeling relieved after silencing critics, again.
Rishabh Pant (Photo/BCCI)
Pant became the only wicketkeeper-batter in the world to complete the SENA set when he reached his ninth Test hundred, and four of them were scored in typical Pant fashion, with a six. He got out looking to go big again, and the naysayers will be out with their swords again, questioning the timing of the hit close to Lunch.
But Pant, being Pant, will shrug off the noise, take fresh guard and again dance down the track, losing grip of the bottom hand while looking to clear the ropes.
Like him or hate him, you can't ignore him.
That's Rishabh Pant for you.

stories.headline: India vs New Zealand 1st Test Day 4: India declare at 720/9, highest team total in New Zealand
stories.deck: India’s 720 for nine was the highest total in a Test innings in New Zealand, eclipsing the home side’s 715 for six declared against Bangladesh at Hamilton in 2019.
stories.bodyText:
India erased several individual and team records before declaring at 720 for nine, giving itself four-and-a-half sessions to bowl New Zealand out in pursuit of a rare Test win in the country.
But it was the first over of the second hour that put the host further on the back foot.
Jasprit Bumrah’s brilliance was on display yet again as it took him just two balls to see the back of New Zealand captain Tom Latham.
Had a close leg-before appeal against Henry Nicholls gone India’s way, the visitor would have been in an even stronger position at tea on the penultimate day at Basin Reserve, with New Zealand struggling at 33 for one in 11 overs, still trailing by 319 runs.
On the first morning, Bumrah had struck off the third ball against Latham. On Sunday, he needed one ball fewer. He began with the same delivery that had accounted for Latham in the first innings, angling it in, before the next moved away just enough. A weary Latham hung his bat out and Rishabh Pant pouched the edge behind the wickets.
Nicholls, who had spent almost the entire week on the field barring five balls, opened his account with a streaky boundary. But he followed it up with a splendid back-foot punch off Bumrah in the latter’s next over, suggesting he was ready to resume his marathon effort after an unbeaten 175 in the first innings.
Nicholls, however, had a close shave in the seventh over when he left a Bumrah inswinger alone. Given not out, he was saved by the umpire’s call on ball-tracking after Shubman Gill opted for a review.
Earlier in the session, India added 91 runs at a brisk pace before Dhruv Jurel was stumped off Glenn Phillips, prompting the declaration.
India’s 720 for nine was the highest total in a Test innings in New Zealand, eclipsing the home side’s 715 for six declared against Bangladesh at Hamilton in 2019. It was also India’s third-highest Test total. India also became the first team to record 50-plus partnerships for each of its first seven wickets in a Test innings, underlining the depth of its batting effort.

stories.headline: Paras Mhambrey set to join Punjab Kings as bowling coach
stories.deck: Paras Mhambrey has signed a contract to become the bowling coach for Punjab Kings in IPL-2027. He previously served as the bowling coach for Mumbai Indians and the Indian cricket team. Mhambrey is recognized for his contributions to bowling strategies during his coaching career. His extensive experience includes coaching domestic teams and participation in international tournaments.
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Former India and 
Mumbai Indians
 bowling coach 
Paras Mhambrey
 is set to join Punjab Kings as their new bowling coach for IPL-2027, TOI has learnt.
Punjab Kings had parted ways with their bowling coach James Hopes recently. Mhambrey will thus chalk out bowling strategies with PBKS head coach 
Ricky Ponting
 and skipper Shreyas Iyer.
"Paras has signed a contract with Punjab Kings today," a source told TOI.
Mhambrey will thus be the second man from MI to join Punjab Kings after Hardik Pandya, who came to the Chandigarh-based franchise through a high-profile trade.
Mhambrey recently parted ways with MI after a long association with the franchise. Mhambrey, who was India's bowling coach from 2022 to 2024 under head coach Rahul Dravid, has had two stints with MI. He was initially with MI since the IPL’s inception in 2008, and then rejoined MI after completing his tenure with the Indian team following the 2024 T20 World Cup triumph.
Mhambrey is currently in Dubai as bowling coach of MI Emirates in the ILT20. He had also coached the India Under-19 team in the 2020 U-19 World Cup in South Africa. During his nearly three-year stint with Team India, the 54-year-old ex-India pacer-turned coach was credited by many, especially ace pacer Mohammed Shami, who kept gesturing towards him from the field during matches, for the Indian bowlers’ brilliant show in the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, and the T20 World Cup in West Indies in June this year.
The Mumbaikar is a product of the BCA-Mafatlal bowling scheme under England fast bowling great Frank Tyson in 1990. He then went on to possess a rich 21-year coaching experience in his CV, a period in which he coached multiple domestic teams, including Bengal, Baroda, Maharashtra and Vidarbha.

stories.headline: Sandpapergate scandal: Lehmann denies knowledge of sandpaper plot, says scandal took him to ‘dark place’
stories.deck: ‘And you know what — I was coach at the time, I’ve got to take that responsibility, so you resign, pushed, whatever you want to call it; it’s so long ago now — we’re talking 8½ years,’ said Darren Lehmann
stories.bodyText:
Former Australian head coach Darren Lehmann has once again denied knowing about his players' plan to use sandpaper on the ball during the infamous Cape Town Test in 2018, saying he has no recollection of being present when the plot was discussed.
Lehmann, who was Australia's head coach at the time, said the ball-tampering scandal took him to a "dark place" mentally.
Asked whether he knew about the use of sandpaper on the field, Lehmann replied: "No. I didn’t know sandpaper was being used. I was coach at the time, I’ve got to take that responsibility."
"I'm sorry for what happened. It's my fault it went too far. At the end of the day, the biggest thing with ball tampering is ... it was a bad time. We all made mistakes," Lehmann was quoted as saying during commentary on ABC Radio for the first T20I between Australia and England in Melbourne.
Lehmann was unable to respond to questions about Cameron Bancroft's claims during commentary on ABC Radio for the third ODI between Australia and England in Hobart on Wednesday and was excused from his commentary duties, according to the 'Sydney Morning Herald'.
In an extraordinary 4,500-word statement on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Bancroft claimed that the entire Australian squad knew about the ball-tampering plot.
Bancroft had alleged that Lehmann and bowling coach David Saker were present during a conversation in Port Elizabeth, the venue of the second Test, in which David Warner proposed using sandpaper to rough up one side of the ball to generate reverse swing.
However, Lehmann said he had no recollection of Warner's proposal.
"I can't remember being present at that conversation. But again [we're discussing a situation from] 8½ years ago ... you'll have to ask those people.
"That's the issue ... I have my version. And that's where I stand."
During the third Test in Cape Town, television footage showed Bancroft concealing sandpaper in his trousers. In his account, Bancroft alleged that Lehmann immediately told Peter Handscomb to "get the sandpaper off Bangers now".
Responding to the allegation, Lehmann said: "I'm not sure. That was all after the fact. It was already played out on TV. That's Cameron's take on it. I'm not going to talk about him, but my view is different."
Cricket Australia's initial investigation in 2018 cleared Lehmann of knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper, but he lost his job as Australia's head coach in the aftermath of the scandal.
Asked whether he had resigned or been sacked, the former Test batter said: "You resign, but the writing was certainly made very clear to me very quickly ... what the consequences are.
"And you know what — I was coach at the time, I've got to take that responsibility, so you resign, pushed, whatever you want to call it. It's so long ago now — we're talking 8½ years. But for me it was the best job in the world. I loved that job."
Lehmann also opened up about the mental toll the scandal took on him.
"I can tell you this and I can tell the listeners – 8½ years ago ... I don't like talking about this scenario," he said.
"I went to a really dark place, mate – as dark a place ... I went to as dark a place as you can think about. It took me ... probably three or four years to actually get back to some sort of normality as such. I'm not going to that dark place (again). I'm trying to move forward. I'm not going back.
"There's things I'll remember and not remember. It's 8½ years ago, a traumatic time. None more so than for my family. And without the support of family and friends back then, I don't know where I'd be."
The 2018 sandpaper scandal was reignited two weeks ago by allegations in the autobiography of Usman Khawaja, who was part of the Australian team in Cape Town. PTI PDS PDS APS

briefs.headline: Unprecedented! Gill's India achieve a first in 149-year history of Test cricket
briefs.deck: The visitors took a lead of 352 runs after New Zealand had been bowled out for 368 in their first innings. India's total of 720 was also the highest team score recorded in New Zealand.
briefs.bodyText:
India became the first team in Test cricket history to record partnerships of 50 or more runs for each of the first seven wickets in an innings as they declared at 720 for nine against New Zealand on day four of the opening Test in Wellington on Sunday.
India declared their innings an hour into the second session, with Dhruv Jurel the last batter to be dismissed. The visitors took a lead of 352 runs after New Zealand had been bowled out for 368 in their first innings. India's total of 720 was also the highest team score recorded in New Zealand.
The first-wicket pair of Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul added 130 runs, followed by a 165-run stand between Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal for the second wicket. Rahul and Shubman Gill then put on 91 runs for the third wicket, before Gill and 
Rishabh Pant
 added 100 for the fourth.
Pant and Anshul Kamboj shared a 68-run partnership for the fifth wicket, while Pant and Jurel added 75 for the sixth. Jurel and Washington Sundar completed the sequence with a 54-run stand for the seventh wicket.
Most 50-plus stands in an innings in Tests
8 - India (innings 1) v England at The Oval, 2007
7 - Australia (innings 2) v England at Sydney, 2025/26
7 - India (innings 2) v New Zealand at Wellington, 2026For the first time in the history of Test cricket, a team has had 50-plus stands for each of the first seven wickets in an innings.
Rahul (136) and Pant (128) scored centuries, while Jaiswal made 85, Padikkal 80, Gill 98 and Jurel 78. Kamboj contributed 38 and Sundar scored 24. Glenn Phillips was New Zealand's most successful bowler, taking three wickets for 154 runs.
Pant also moved to second place on the list of most sixes in Test cricket during his century. He went past former New Zealand batter Brendon McCullum, taking his tally to 108, one more than McCullum's 107. England's Ben Stokes leads the list with 138 sixes.
Pant struck 10 fours and six sixes in his 128 off 153 balls. During the innings, he also became the sixth Indian batter, after Sachin Tendulkar, Mohammed Azharuddin, Rahul Dravid, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul, to score a Test century in all four SENA countries.

briefs.headline: 720/9! Team India rewrite record books, post highest-ever Test total in NZ
briefs.deck: India's 720/9 became the biggest total ever scored in a Test innings on New Zealand soil. The previous best was the hosts' 715/6 declared against Bangladesh in Hamilton in 2019. India also broke the record for the highest Test total against New Zealand. The West Indies had earlier held the record with their 660/5 declared at the Basin Reserve in Wellington in 1995.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India delivered a remarkable batting performance against New Zealand in the first Test at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Sunday. The visitors declared their innings at 720/9 on Day 4, building a massive 352-run lead.
In the process, India registered the highest-ever team total in a Test innings in New Zealand. They broke the previous record of 715/6 declared, which the hosts had scored against Bangladesh in Hamilton in 2019.
KL Rahul and Rishabh Pant were the stars with the bat, scoring 136 and 128 respectively. Glenn Phillips was the most successful New Zealand bowler, finishing with figures of 3/154.
India declared their innings around an hour before tea, with Dhruv Jurel being the last batter to get out. New Zealand had scored 368 in their first innings, leaving them with a huge challenge after India's batting effort.
India set new record for highest Test total in New Zealand
India's 720/9 became the biggest total ever scored in a Test innings on New Zealand soil. The previous best was the hosts' 715/6 declared against Bangladesh in Hamilton in 2019.
India also broke the record for the highest Test total against New Zealand. The West Indies had earlier held the record with their 660/5 declared at the Basin Reserve in Wellington in 1995.
India's highest Test totals against New Zealand
- 720/9 declared – Wellington, 2026 (Won)
- 583/7 declared – Ahmedabad, 1999 (Draw)
- 566/8 declared – Nagpur, 2010 (Won)
- 557/5 declared – Indore, 2016 (Won)
- 537/3 declared – Chennai, 1956 (Won)
India had crossed 500 runs in a Test innings in New Zealand only once before this match. They scored 520 all out against the hosts in Hamilton in 2009.
Six consecutive 50-plus partnerships
India's innings also featured a rare batting record. Each of their first six partnerships added at least 50 runs.
This has happened only four times in Test cricket. Australia first achieved it against West Indies in Brisbane in 1960-61. Pakistan followed with a similar effort against Bangladesh in Khulna in 2015.
India also managed the feat against Australia in Ahmedabad in 2023. Their performance in Wellington makes them the first team to achieve it twice.
Another unusual record came from India's top five batters, with each of them scoring at least 80 runs. This has happened only twice in Test cricket.
The previous occasion was in 2014, when Pakistan's top five all scored 80 or more in their innings of 566/3 declared against New Zealand in Abu Dhabi.
India second on list of most 700-plus Test totals
India's 720/9 was their fifth 700-plus score in Test cricket. They now occupy the second position on the list of teams with the most 700-plus totals.
Sri Lanka lead the chart with seven such scores. India have five, while England, Australia and West Indies have four each.
Most 700-plus totals in Test cricket
- 7 – Sri Lanka
- 5 – India
- 4 – England
- 4 – Australia
- 4 – West Indies
- 2 – Pakistan
- 1 – New Zealand
India's third-highest Test total
The 720-run effort in Wellington is now India's third-highest total in Test cricket.
Their biggest score remains 759/7 declared against England in Chennai in 2016. The second-highest is 726/9 declared against Sri Lanka at the Brabourne Stadium in 2009.
India's highest innings totals in Test cricket
- 759/7 declared vs England – Chennai, 2016
- 726/9 declared vs Sri Lanka – Brabourne, 2009
- 720/9 declared vs New Zealand – Wellington, 2026
- 707 vs Sri Lanka – Colombo (SSC), 2010
- 705/7 declared vs Australia – Sydney, 2004

briefs.headline: From practice to performance: Gagan Narang aims to bring data into India’s shooting ecosystem
briefs.deck: Gagan Narang, the 2012 London Olympics medallist, has done plenty to give back to the sport. He's built academies and nurtured athletes. His latest endeavour is a training diary that can help shooters identify patterns, improve preparation and bridge the information gap between grassroots athletes and the elite.
briefs.bodyText:
New Delhi:
 In shooting, where medals can be decided by fractions, consistency is often the difference between success and failure. Yet, while athletes spend hours perfecting their technique, not everyone systematically records their training or tracks their progress.
That is the gap Gagan Narang hopes to address through ABHYAS (A Blueprint of Honing Your Accuracy in Shooting), a training diary designed to help shooters document their sessions, identify patterns and make their preparation more scientific.
“Most Indian shooters train hard but train without a record. A shooter in a small town may fire thousands of shots a month, and a year later, neither the athlete nor the coach can say what changed, what worked and what did not. Memory is a poor coach,” Narang told TimesofIndia.com.
ABHYAS allows shooters to log what they trained, the number of shots fired, scores, how they felt and observations from each session. Over time, these entries can offer a clearer picture of an athlete's development, helping coaches assess performances and provide guidance based on evidence rather than recollection.
Science in sport begins with measurement, and measurement begins with the habit of writing things down. At the elite level, that habit exists, supported by data systems and support teams. At the grassroots level, it almost never does.
Gagan Narang
The initiative is part of Project Amarjeet, established by Narang and Olympian and Arjuna Awardee Anuraj Singh in memory of Narang’s mother, Amarjit Narang. 
The launch coincided with her birth anniversary, giving the initiative a personal significance for the family.
“Abhyas is a training diary built for shooters. After every session, the athlete logs what they trained, how many shots, the scores, how they felt and what they noticed. Over weeks, those entries become a picture of the athlete. A coach can look at that picture, even from another city, and give guidance based on evidence instead of a conversation at the end of a tiring day. Abhyas means practice, and the idea is simple: practice that is recorded can be improved,” he added.
The emphasis is on making sports science accessible beyond the elite level, where athletes often have access to specialised teams and data systems.
“Science in sport begins with measurement, and measurement begins with the habit of writing things down. At the elite level, that habit exists, supported by data systems and support teams. At the grassroots level, it almost never does. Abhyas gives a young shooter that habit for free,” Narang said.
By recording their sessions, shooters can identify recurring patterns, such as scores dropping towards the end of practice or performances being affected by poor sleep. A weakness that may otherwise appear subjective can become something measurable. Coaches handling multiple athletes can also use these records to monitor individual trends, with a phone being the only requirement.
Building beyond individual performances
India's shooting ecosystem has evolved over the past decade, with more ranges, academies, competitions, better equipment and athletes proving they can win at the highest level. Narang believes the growing acceptance of shooting as a career has also played a role.
“Parents now see shooting as a real career, and that belief changes everything,” he said.
However, sustaining India's progress requires attention to the grassroots rather than just its medal-winning athletes.
We need coaches who keep learning. We need athletes supported in the whole of life, including the mind, the body, nutrition, studies, money and the parents who stand behind them. And we need continuity, so that a good programme does not end when a person changes jobs.
Gagan Narang
“Medals at the Olympics are the visible part, but they come from thousands of young shooters training in ordinary conditions. If we look after that base, with access to pellets, coaching, guidance and information, the top will take care of itself. Progress that depends on a few brilliant individuals is fragile. Progress that depends on a strong system lasts,” Narang said.
Turning individual success into sustained dominance, he believes, requires a structured pathway for athletes, continued learning among coaches and support extending beyond training.
“Consistency. Individual brilliance happens when talent meets opportunity. Dominance happens when that meeting is repeated year after year, by design and not by luck. For that, we need a clear pathway from the first shot to the podium, where every athlete knows the next step. We need coaches who keep learning. We need athletes supported in the whole of life, including the mind, the body, nutrition, studies, money and the parents who stand behind them. And we need continuity, so that a good programme does not end when a person changes jobs. Too often, we rebuild from zero. The countries that dominate a sport build once and then improve every year,” he said.
Better governance is not an administrative luxury. It decides how many talented young people get a real chance, so in the end, it shows up in results.
Gagan Narang
Narang's experience as an athlete and administrator, currently the Vice President of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and named in the electoral college for the upcoming elections, has also shaped his views on sports governance, particularly the need for transparency, accountability and continuity in decision-making.
“An athlete can accept a hard decision. What an athlete cannot accept is a decision nobody explains. Transparency means selection criteria are known in advance and followed. Accountability means those who make decisions are answerable for them. Continuity means a good policy survives a change of office bearers,” he said.
He believes better governance can build confidence among athletes and parents, while also encouraging sponsors to invest in a system they trust.
“Better governance is not an administrative luxury. It decides how many talented young people get a real chance, so in the end, it shows up in results,” Narang added.
Abhyas may be a simple intervention, but it reflects a larger philosophy: progress in sport is not driven by talent and hard work alone. Access, structure, information and the ability to learn from every training session can be equally important.
For India's shooting ambitions, the next step may not always be about firing more shots. It could be about understanding every shot better.

briefs.headline: Rishabh Pant becomes first Indian wicketkeeper to achieve this rare feat
briefs.deck: Rishabh Pant achieved a remarkable milestone by scoring Test centuries in all four SENA countries. His latest contribution was a century against New Zealand in Wellington. This century marked his return to international cricket after a brief injury hiatus. Pant is now the third Indian wicketkeeper to attain nine Test centuries. He has also surpassed Brendon McCullum in the list of most sixes in…
briefs.bodyText:
Rishabh Pant
 added another special achievement to his name on Sunday, becoming the first Indian wicketkeeper to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries - South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.
The left-handed batter reached the milestone with an attacking century on Day 4 of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.
Pant, 29, was playing his first match for India since the tour of Sri Lanka in August. He brought up his hundred in just 135 balls. At 99, he played a cheeky reverse-sweep off part-time spinner Glenn Phillips, sending the ball past short third man. On the very next delivery, he stepped down the track and hit Phillips over mid-off for a six to complete his century.
Pant was eventually caught at deep midwicket for 128 off 153 balls. However, his knock had helped India take a 261-run lead by the lunch break.
Joins an elite list
Pant became only the sixth Indian batter to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries. The other five are Mohammad Azharuddin, Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul.
Rahul entered the list a day earlier, becoming the first Indian opener to achieve the feat.
Asian batters with Test centuries in all four SENA countries:
- Mohammad Azharuddin
- Sachin Tendulkar
- Saeed Anwar
- Rahul Dravid
- Younis Khan
- Kumar Sangakkara
- Virat Kohli
- KL Rahul
- Rishabh Pant
Pakistan's Saeed Anwar and Younis Khan, along with Sri Lanka's Kumar Sangakkara, are the other Asian batters to have achieved this feat.
Among wicketkeepers from around the world, only Australia's Adam Gilchrist and England's Jonny Bairstow have also scored Test hundreds in all four SENA countries.
Third on the list of most Test hundreds by wicketkeepers
The Wellington century was Pant's ninth in Test cricket as a designated wicketkeeper. He is now third on the all-time list, behind Gilchrist (17) and Zimbabwe's Andy Flower (12).
Seven of Pant's nine Test hundreds have come outside India. He also became the first Indian wicketkeeper to score a Test century in New Zealand.
Most Test centuries as a designated wicketkeeper
- 17 – Adam Gilchrist
- 12 – Andy Flower
- 9 – Rishabh Pant
- 8 – Les Ames
A look at Pant's SENA centuries
Pant's journey of scoring Test hundreds in all four SENA countries began with a 114-run knock at The Oval in 2018.
He followed it with an unbeaten 159 against Australia in Sydney in 2019. That remains his highest Test score.
In January 2022, he scored an unbeaten 100 in Cape Town against South Africa. Later that year, he hit 146 against England at Edgbaston.
Last year, Pant continued his good run in England, scoring 134 and 118 at Leeds.
Pant shows no signs of rust after injury break
Pant's return to international cricket was closely watched after he missed India's entire four-day series against New Zealand A due to a left-side strain.
Before that, he had led Rest of India in the Irani Cup match against Ranji Trophy champions Jammu & Kashmir in Srinagar in October.
However, he looked in excellent touch in Wellington and showed no signs of being short of match practice.
Pant scored most of his runs on the leg side, using his trademark slog sweeps and powerful shots. He often moved his front leg out of the way to open up the leg-side field and played several shots behind square. He also used his feet well to hit the ball over the bowler's head.
Moves past McCullum in Test sixes list
Pant's attacking century also helped him move past former New Zealand captain Brendon McCullum in the list of most sixes in Test cricket.
He now has 108 sixes, putting him second on the list behind England captain Ben Stokes, who has 138.
Most sixes in Test cricket
- 138 – Ben Stokes (Balls per six: 90.05)

briefs.headline: Pant goes on rampage, edges past McCullum in list of most sixes in Test cricket
briefs.deck: Pant struck 10 fours and six sixes during his 128 off 153 balls, taking his tally of sixes in Test cricket to 108. McCullum had hit 107, while England's Ben Stokes tops the list with 138 sixes.
briefs.bodyText:
Rishabh Pant
 moved to second place on the list of most sixes in Test cricket, going past former New Zealand batter 
Brendon McCullum
, as he scored his ninth Test century to help India reach 629 for six at lunch on day four of the opening Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve.
Pant struck 10 fours and six sixes during his 128 off 153 balls, taking his tally of sixes in Test cricket to 108. McCullum had hit 107, while England's 
Ben Stokes
 tops the list with 138 sixes.
Most sixes in Test cricket
Pant's innings helped India extend their lead to 261 runs by lunch on day four. The visitors added 143 runs in the session after taking control of the match on day three.
During his knock, Pant also became the sixth Indian batter, after Sachin Tendulkar, Mohammed Azharuddin, Rahul Dravid, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul, to score a Test century in all four SENA countries. He is also the first Asian wicketkeeper to achieve the feat.

- Saeed Anwar

- Kumar Sangakkara

- Rishabh Pant
Pant began the day cautiously but changed gears after lofting Kyle Jamieson over long-on and sending the ball into the Basin Reserve car park. He then took on off-spinner Glenn Phillips, reaching 99 with a reverse sweep before dancing down the track to hit him over the infield and complete his century.
It was the fourth time Pant had reached a Test hundred with a six. He finished with 10 fours and six sixes, sticking to his attacking style despite criticism in recent weeks.
Pant's innings was also significant given that he had been out of competitive cricket for seven weeks. He missed the India A matches as well because the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru had not declared him fit to play.
There had been questions over whether Pant was ready for a Test match, but his wicketkeeping and batting in the ongoing game have addressed concerns about his form and fitness.

briefs.headline: NWSL Championship: Kelce backs Kansas City Current; club seeks first title
briefs.deck: Travis Kelce has publicly backed Patrick Mahomes’ Kansas City Current ahead of the 2026 NWSL Championship final. Speaking on his New Heights podcast, the Chiefs tight end wished the team luck and hoped they would bring home the trophy. Mahomes and his wife, Brittany, are part of the club’s ownership group. Kansas City reached the final after defeating Gotham FC 2-1 in the semi-finals.
briefs.bodyText:
Patrick Mahomes
 and 
Brittany Mahomes
 have another reason to feel proud of their Kansas City sports family. As the Kansas City Current prepare for a major test in the 2026 NWSL Championship, they have received a show of support from an unexpected but familiar face. Kansas City Chiefs star 
Travis Kelce
 has joined the growing list of people cheering for the club, sending a short message that carries plenty of meaning. With the team chasing its first NWSL title, the encouragement comes at an important moment in its season.
Travis Kelce sends a message to Patrick Mahomes’ Kansas City Current
Kelce made his support clear during the latest episode of his 
New Heights
 podcast. The Chiefs tight end did not deliver a lengthy speech or make a big show of his involvement. Instead, he offered a few simple words for the team as it prepared for the championship clash.
"Current going to the championship. Wish them the best of luck. And they bring it home," Kelce said.
The message reflected the close sporting connections within Kansas City. Although Kelce spends most of his time focused on the NFL, his support for the Current highlights how the city's teams have built a shared identity.
The club also acknowledged the Chiefs star's gesture on social media. The Current highlighted Kelce wearing their Storm Kit, giving fans another glimpse of the support the women's team receives from prominent figures across the city's sporting community.
For the Current, the attention comes as they prepare for one of the biggest matches in the club's history. They previously reached the NWSL Championship final in 2022 but finished runners-up after losing 2-0 to the Portland Thorns. This time, they have another opportunity to turn a strong playoff campaign into silverware.
Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have a personal stake in the NWSL final
Kelce's message also draws attention to Mahomes' connection with the Kansas City Current. The Chiefs quarterback joined the club's ownership group in January 2023, while his wife, Brittany, had already been involved in its ownership structure.
Their investment reflects a wider commitment to growing women's football and strengthening the club's position in the NWSL. Mahomes has also publicly encouraged the players before the final, urging them to play with confidence, stay true to themselves and bring the championship back to Kansas City.
The Current earned their place in the title match with a 2-1 semi-final victory over Gotham FC, the 2026 NWSL Shield winners. It was a significant result against one of the league's strongest sides.
Kansas City now face the Washington Spirit at Audi Field in Washington, D.C. The Spirit are competing in their third consecutive championship final, making the challenge even tougher.
The match is scheduled for 8 p.m. ET on Saturday, November 21, with coverage on CBS and Paramount+. With Mahomes and Kelce among those backing the club, the Current will be hoping to make this championship appearance count and deliver a historic first NWSL title.

briefs.headline: Arsenal held to 2-2 draw by Newcastle
briefs.deck: In a see-saw final period, neither side ⁠could find the net again, and the draw moved champions Arsenal to ‌28 points, six clear of Brighton & Hove Albion
briefs.bodyText:
Arsenal missed the chance to go eight points clear at the top of the Premier League as they were held to a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United on Saturday (November 21, 2026), with Mikel Arteta's side having to fight back from 2-1 down after a spirited display from their hosts.
Also read | Mikel Arteta signs new contract at Arsenal to 2030 after leading club to Premier League title
Arsenal looked set for an easy evening in the first half and they took the lead in the 33rd minute, Eberechi Eze latching on to a superb angled pass from Kai Havertz to sweep the ball into the net.
Booed off at the break, Newcastle levelled four minutes into the second half as Martin Odegaard was robbed from a throw-in by William Osula. The Danish striker fed the ball to Harvey Barnes, who took a touch before rifling the ball past the keeper.
In the 62nd minute the home side went ahead, Malick Thiaw bundling the ball into the net from close range after Arsenal failed to clear a corner. Arsenal keeper David Raya then suffered an arm injury and was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.
Arteta's side clawed their way back into the game in the 78th minute, Noni Madueke crowning a sweeping Arsenal attack with a left-foot shot, but keeper Lukas Hornicek should have done more to keep it out.
In a see-saw final period, neither side could find the net again, and the draw moved champions Arsenal to 28 points, six clear of Brighton & Hove Albion, who can close the gap at Hull City on Sunday (November 22, 2026).
